(ता), m. any divinity who averts evil. —शान्ति-कर्मन्, अ, n. any action leading to tranquillity or for averting evil. —शान्ति-काम, अस्, m. desire of tranquillity; (अस्, आ, अम्), desirous of tranquillity. —शान्ति-गृह, अम्, n. a room for rest or retirement near the place of sacrifice. —शान्ति-चन्द्रिका, f., N. of a poem by Kavi-candra. —शान्-ति-जल, अम्, n. = शान्त्य्-उद. —शान्ति-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving tranquillity, tranquillizing. —शान्ति-देवा, f., N. of a daughter of Devaka. —शान्ति-पर्वन्, अ, n. ‘Tranquillizing-section,’ N. of the twelfth book of the Mahā-bhārata, (the longest in the whole poem and consisting chiefly of stories, discourses, and epi-sodes narrated for the tranquillizing of the troubled spirit of Yudhi-ṣṭhira after the termination of the war and the slaughter of his many relatives.) —शान्ति-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of a Jaina work by Aśaga. —शान्ति-रत्न, अम्, n. ‘jewel of tranquillity,’ N. of a work. —शान्ति-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a particular religious observance (kept on the fifth day of the light half of the month Kārttika). —शान्ति-शतक, अम्, n. ‘a hundred verses on tranquillity,’ N. of a short poem by Śrī-śihlana. —शान्ति-शील, अस्, m. ‘quiet-tempered,’ a proper N. —शान्ति-सर्वस्व, अम्, n. ‘essence of quietism,’ N. of a work. —शान्ति-सूक्त, अम्, n., N. of a hymn on quietism. —शान्ति-सूरि, इस्, m., N. of the author of a Jaina work. —शान्ति-होम, अस्, m. a propitiatory oblation, a burnt offering to avert or remedy evil. —शान्त्य्-उद or शान्त्य्-उदक, अम्, n. propitiatory water, water offered at sacrifices for propitiation, lustral water. —शान्त्युद-कुम्भ, अस्, m. a vessel holding propitiatory water.
शान्तिक: शान्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, propitiatory, expiatory; pro-ducing ease or quiet; relating to quiet, &c.; (अम्), n. observances or ceremonies for the removal of calamities. —शान्तिक-कर्मन्, अ, n. a magic rite performed for removing obstacles; [cf. शान्ति-कर्-मन्।]
शान्त्वा: शान्त्वा, ind. = शमित्वा, having been tranquil.
शान्तनु: शान्तनु शान्तनु, उस्, m. (fr. शन्तनु?), the twenty-first sovereign of the lunar dynasty in the Dvāpara or third age, (he was son of Pratīpa and was father of Bhīṣma by Gaṅgā before he became the father of Vicitra-vīrya by his wife Satya-vatī.)
शान्तनव: शान्तनव, अस्, m. (fr. शान्तनु above), a patro-nymic of Bhīṣma (as son of king Śāntanu, the re-puted great-uncle of the Pāṇḍavas); N. of the author of the Phiṭ-sūtras on accentuation; (ई), f., scil. टीका, the commentary composed by Śantanu. —शान्तन-वाचार्य (°व-आच्°), अस्, m. the author of the Phiṭ-sūtras.
शान्त्व्: शान्त्व् शान्त्व् (probably connected with rt. 1. शम्; by some regarded as a Nom. fr. शान्त्व below; frequently, but less correctly, written सान्त्व्), cl. 10. P. A. शान्त्वयति, -ते, अशशान्त्वत्, शान्त्वयितुम्, to console, comfort, soothe, coax, pacify, conciliate; to address gently or kindly.
शान्त्व: शान्त्व, अम्, n. (less correctly written सान्त्व), con-solation, consoling, comforting; conciliation; mild-ness; mild speech; gentle or peaceable means. —शान्त्व-पूर्वम्, ind. in a conciliatory manner, coaxingly, (see पूर्व।) —शान्त्व-वाद, अस्, आ, अम्, speaking in a kindly and affectionate manner.
शान्त्वन: शान्त्वन, अम्, n. (less correctly written सान्त्वन), the act of appeasing or reconciling, conciliation, reconcilement; mildness; (at the end of an adj. comp.) appeasing; (आ, अम्), f. n. speaking kindly and in a conciliatory manner; friendly salutation and inquiry; (आनि), n. pl. kind or flattering words.
शान्त्वयत्: शान्त्वयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, consoling, appeasing.
शान्त्वयित्वा: शान्त्वयित्वा, ind. having consoled or comforted.
शान्त्वित: शान्त्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, consoled, comforted.
शान्त्व्य: शान्त्व्य (anom. ind. part.), having consoled or comforted.
शान्त्वति: शान्त्वति शान्त्वति, इस्, f. a kind of plant or shrub (= ब्राह्मण-यष्टिका).
शाप: शाप शाप, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. शप्), curse, ana-thema, execration, cursing, reviling; abuse; oath, imprecation, affirmation by oath or ordeal; ban, interdiction. —शाप-ग्रस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, seized by a curse, suffering under a curse. —शाप-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, arising from a curse. —शाप-नाशन, अस्, m., N. of a Muni. —शाप-प्रद, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘curse-giving,’ uttering imprecations. —शाप-भीत, अस्, आ, अम्, dreading a curse. —शाप-मुक्त, अस्, आ, अम्, released from a curse. —शाप-मुक्ति, इस्, f. or शाप-मोक्ष, अस्, m. deliverance from a curse. —शाप-यन्-त्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, restrained by a curse. —शापान्त (°प-अन्°) or शापावसान (°प-अव्°), अस्, m. the end of a curse or of the period during which an im-precation takes effect. —शापास्त्र (°प-अस्°), अस्, m. ‘having curses for weapons,’ a Muni, saint, (a curse pronounced by a Muni being formidable even to the deities.) —शापोत्सर्ग (°प-उत्°), अस्, m. ‘pouring out a curse,’ the uttering of an imprecation. —शा-पोद्धार (°प-उद्°), अस्, m. deliverance from a curse.
शापित: शापित, अस्, आ, अम्, made to take an oath, one to whom an oath has been administered, sworn, adjured, proved by ordeal.
शापेय: शापेय, see Gaṇa Śaunakādi to Pāṇ. IV. 3, 106.
शापेयिन्: शापेयिन्, ई, m. a proper N.; (इनस्), m. pl., N. of a school of the White Yajur-veda.
शापठिक: शापठिक शापठिक, अस्, m. a peacock.
शाफरिक: शाफरिक शाफरिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शफर), relating to the Śaphara fish; (अस्), m. a fisherman.
शाफेय: शाफेय शाफेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Śākhā of the Yajur-veda; [cf. शापेय।]
शाबर: शाबर शाबर, अस्, m., N. of the commen-tary written by Śabara-svāmin; of a work by Prāṇa-kṛṣṇa; of a Tantra work ascribed to Śiva. —शाबर-भाष्य, अम्, n. the commentary written by Śabara-svāmin.
शाब्द: शाब्द शाब्द, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शब्द), sonorous, sounding; relating to sound, (opposed to आर्थ, q. v.); relating to or derived from words; verbal, oral; nominal (as inflection); (अस्), m. a philologist, grammarian; (ई), f. Sarasvatī (as goddess of speech and eloquence). —शाब्द-बोध, अस्, m. ‘verbal knowledge,’ apprehension of the meaning of words, perception of the verbal or literal sense (of a sen-tence, &c.). —शाब्द-व्यञ्जना, f. (in rhetoric) suggestion or insinuation founded on words (as op-posed to आर्थ-व्यञ्जना or suggestion dependent upon the meaning of words).
शाब्दिक: शाब्दिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to sounds or words; making a noise, sounding; verbal; (अस्), m. one skilled in words, a philologist, grammarian. —शाब्-दिक-नरसिंह, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
शाम: शाम शाम, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. rt. 1. शम्), Ved. appeasing, curing, having curative properties.
शामन्: शामन्, अ, n. [cf. सामन्], appeasing, reconciling, reconciliation, conciliation.
शामन: शामन, अस्, m. one who ‘settles’ or destroys, N. of Yama (= शमन); (अम्), n. conciliation; tranquillity, peace; settling, killing, slaughter; end, (शामनं या, to go to an end, be destroyed); (ई), f. the southern quarter.
शामलदास: शामल-दास or शामल-भट्ट, अस्, m., N. of a modern poet.
शामित्र: शामित्र, अम्, n. a sacrificial vessel; a hearth or place (for cooking a sacrificial animal); a deadly blow; sacrificing; tying up cattle for sacrifice, &c.
शामुल्य: शामुल्य, अम्, n. (probably connected with श-मल), Ved. (perhaps) anything requiring cleansing or expiation (as a dirty or defiled garment; according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda X. 85, 29 = शमलं शारीरं शरीर-छिन्नस्य मलस्य धारकं वस्त्रम्).
शामूल: शामूल, अम्, n., Ved. (according to some) an old woollen garment.
शाम्ब: शाम्ब शाम्ब, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa and Jāmbavatī (frequently mentioned in the Purāṇas and in the Mausala-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata, where it is related that in consequence of the curse of some holy sages who had been deceived by a female disguise he had assumed, he was condemned to produce offspring in the shape of a terrific iron club for the destruction of the race of Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka; he is said to have been instructed by Nārada in the proper worship of the sun, and by Vyāsa in the ritual observances of the Magi; he is regarded as the author of the Sūrya-stotra hymn). —शाम्ब-पुर, अम्, n. or शाम्ब-पुरी, f., N. of a city founded by Śāmba (said to be situated on the banks of the Candra-bhāgā). —शाम्ब-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of a Purāṇa. —शाम्बादित्य (°ब-आद्°), अस्, m. a particular form of the sun. —शाम्बोप-पुराण (°ब-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
शाम्बरिक: शाम्बरिक शाम्बरिक, अस्, m. a proper N.
शाम्बरी: शाम्बरी शाम्बरी, f. (fr. शम्बर), jugglery, sorcery, illusion (as practised by the Daitya Śambara); a sorceress.
शाम्बविक: शाम्बविक शाम्बविक, अस्, m. (fr. शम्बु), a worker or dealer in shells.
शाम्बुक: शाम्बुक, अस्, m. a bivalve shell; [cf. शम्बुक।]
शाम्बुवि: शाम्बुवि, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a Śākhā or school.
शाम्बूक: शाम्बूक, अस्, m. a bivalve shell.
शाम्भर: शाम्भर शाम्भर, N. of a city in Ajmere (commonly called Sāmbhar or Sāmbher, where a par-ticular kind of fossil salt is found). —शाम्भर-नगर, अम्, n. the city of Śāmbhara.
शाम्भरायणी: शाम्भरायणी, f., N. of a woman, (also written साम्भरायणी।)
शाम्भव: शाम्भव शाम्भव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शम्भु), belonging to Śiva; (अस्), m. a worshipper of Śiva; the son of Śambhu; camphor; a sort of poison; a kind of plant (= शिव-मल्ली); bdellium (= गुग्-गुलु); (ई), f., N. of Pārvatī; a kind of plant (= नील-दूर्वा); the aperture through which the soul is said to escape (= मुद्रा-मार्ग); (अम्), n. the Deva-dāru. —शाम्भव-देव, अस्, m., N. of a poet.
शाय: शाय शाय, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. शी), lying, sleeping.
शायक: 1. शायक, अस्, इका, अम्, lying, sleeping, reposing; (इका), f. sleeping, repose, sleep.
शायक 2. शायक, अस्, m. (fr. rt. शो), an arrow; a sword; [cf. सायक।]
शायिन्: शायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, lying down, reclining, sleeping, resting, abiding, (अधः-शायिन्, sleeping on the ground; एक-शायिन्, sleeping alone.)
शार्: शार् शार् (also written सार्), cl. 10. P. शारयति, -यितुम्, to be weak or feeble; to weaken; [cf. rt. शॄ।]
शार: शार शार, अस्, ई, अम्, (in some senses fr. rt. शॄ; in others fr. शृ substituted for rt. सृ), varie-gated (in colour), of different colours (as dark hair mixed with grey); mottled, spotted; yellow; (अस्), m. hurting, injuring; variegating; a variegated colour; a mixture of blue and yellow, green; air, wind, (perhaps for सार); a chess-man, piece used at chess or at a kind of backgammon, (for सार, q. v.); (ई), f., Ved. an arrow; Kuśa grass; (अम्), n. a variegated colour. —शार-ता, f. or शार-त्व, अम्, n. variety of colour, yellowness.
शारङ्ग: शारङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम् [cf. सारङ्ग], of a variegated colour, spotted, dappled; (अस्), m. the Cātaka bird, Cuculus Melanoleucus; a peacock; a bee; a deer; an elephant; (ई), f. a particular musical instrument, a stringed instrument played with a bow, a sort of fiddle; N. of the wife of Manda-pāla.
शारि: शारि, इस्, m. a chess-man, piece at chess (or at a kind of draughts); a little round ball (= गुटिका); a kind of die; (इस्), f. a kind of bird, (see शारिका); an elephant's housings or armour; fraud, trick. —शारि-पट्ट, अस्, m. or शारि-फल, अम्, n. or शारि-फ-लक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a chequered cloth or table for playing draughts, &c. —शारि-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a disciple of Buddha. —शारि-शृङ्खला, f. a sort of die for playing at draughts, &c.
शारिका: शारिका, f. a kind of bird (commonly called Maina, either the Gracula Religiosa or the Turdus Salica, cf. सारिका); a bow or stick used for playing the Vīṇā or any stringed instrument; chess-playing; a piece or man at chess or backgammon (according to some); N. of the tutelary goddess of Śārīṭaka.
शारित: शारित, अस्, आ, अम्, variegated, coloured.
शारिवा: शारिवा, f. a particular plant (the root of which is used medicinally as a substitute for sarsaparilla, = श्यामा, अनन्त-मूल, उत्पल-शारिवा, cf. सारिवा).
शारी: शारी, f. a kind of bird (= शारिका); = कुशा (ac-cording to Śabda-k.).
शारुक: शारुक, अस्, ई, अम्, one who injures or destroys (with acc.); mischievous, noxious, injurious.
शारद: शारद शारद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शरद्), autumnal, produced or growing in autumn; annual, lasting for a year or from year to year, perennial (said of the cities of the Asuras); new, recent [cf. रज्जु-शा-रद]; modest, diffident; belonging to the Asura Śarad (according to Sāy.); (अस्), m. autumnal sick-ness; autumnal sunshine; a year; a sort of kidney-bean (yellow Mūng and another kind, = पीत-मुद्ग, हरिन्-मुद्ग); a kind of plant (= कास); the Vakula tree; (औ), m. du., scil. मासौ, the two months of autumn (Ved.); (आ), f., N. of Sarasvatī; of Durgā; of a daughter of Deva-ratha; a kind of musical instrument, a sort of Vīṇā or lute; N. of certain plants (= ब्राह्मी, सारिवा); = शारदा-तिलक below; (ई), f. the plant Jussiæa Repens; the Sapta-parṇa tree; the day of full moon in the month Kārttika or (according to some) Āśvina, = कोजागर-पूर्णिमा; (अम्), n. corn, grain, fruit (as ripening in the autumn); the white lotus. —शारदा-तिलक, अम्, n., N. of a mystical poem by Lakṣmaṇa; of a drama by Śaṅkara. —शारदा-तिलक-तन्त्र, अम्, n. the Tantra called Śāradā-tilaka. —शारदाम्बा (°दा-अम्°), f. the goddess Śāradā, i. e. Sarasvatī.
शारदिक: शारदिक, अम्, n. a particular funeral ceremony, an annual or autumnal Śrāddha; (अस्), m. autumnal sickness; heat or sunshine in autumn.
शारदिन्: शारदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, autumnal, belonging to autumn.
शारदीय: शारदीय, अस्, ई, अम्, autumnal. —शारदीय-म-हापूजा, f. the autumnal great worship (of Durgā).
शारद्वत: शारद्वत, अस्, ई, अम्, of or belonging to Śarad-vat, descended from Śarad-vat; (अस्), m. a proper N. —शारद्वती-पुत्र, अस्, m. a proper N.
शाराव: शाराव शाराव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शराव), placed on a shallow dish (as rice &c.).
शारीटक: शारीटक शारीटक, N. of a town of Kaśmīra.
शारीर: शारीर शारीर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शरीर), cor-poreal, bodily, relating to the body (of animals); belonging to or produced from the body; connected with the body, incorporate; (अम्), n. the incor-porate soul or spirit; a particular drug (= वृष, which may mean ‘a bull,’ ‘a kind of drug,’ &c.); ex-crement, excretion; (अस्), m. corporal punishment (?). —शारीर-व्रण, अस्, m. a bodily ulcer or tumour.
शारीरक: शारीरक, अस्, ई, अम्, corporeal, relating to the body; incorporate; (अम्), n. the soul or embodied spirit or the doctrine inquiring into the nature of the embodied spirit; N. of Śaṅkarācārya's commen-tary on the Vedānta or Brahma-sūtras. —शारीरक-टीका, f., N. of a work by Vācas-pati. —शारीरक-मीमांसा, f. an inquiry into the embodied spirit (= ब्रह्म-मीमांसा, उत्तर-मीमांसा, वेदान्त, q. q. v. v.). —शारीरक-मीमांसा-भाष्य, अम्, n., N. of a commentary by Rāmānuja on the Brahma-sūtras; of another by Śaṅkarācārya. —शारीरक-सूत्र, अम्, n. the aphorisms of the Vedānta philo-sophy (= ब्रह्म-सूत्र, q. v.).
शारीरकीय: शारीरकीय, अस्, ई, अम्, corporeal, psychological (as a book treating of the incorporate soul).
शारीरिक: शारीरिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to the body, cor-poreal, personal, material, contained in the body, incorporate, psychological.
शार्क: शार्क शार्क, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शॄ, con-nected with शर्करा, q. v.), clayed or candied sugar.
शार्कक: शार्कक, अस्, m. clayed or candied sugar; a lump of sugar; a lump or ball of meat; the froth of milk, syllabub; cream.

शार्करक: शार्करक or शार्करिक, अस्, ई, अम्, gravelly, stony, &c.; (अस्), m. a place abounding in stones or gravel.
शार्कराक्ष: शार्कराक्ष, अस्, m. (probably fr. शर्कराक्ष), a patronymic.
शार्कराक्षि: शार्कराक्षि, अयस्, m. pl., N. of a Gotra.
शार्करीय: शार्करीय, अस्, ई, अम्, stony, gravelly, &c.
शार्गाल: शार्गाल शार्गाल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शृगाल), of or belonging to a jackal.
शार्ङ्ग: शार्ङ्ग शार्ङ्ग, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शृङ्ग), made of horn, horny, corneous; (अस्), m. a bow, (accord-ing to some अम्, n.); N. of the bow of Viṣṇu; N. of a bird; a patronymic of several Vedic Ṛṣis; (अम्), n. ginger (= आर्द्रक). —शार्ङ्ग-देव, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Saṅgīta-ratnākara. —शार्ङ्ग-धन्वन्, आ, m. epithet of Viṣṇu. —शार्ङ्ग-धर, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Vaidya-vallabha; of the author of the works mentioned below. —शार्ङ्गधर-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of an anthology of didactic verses. —शार्ङ्गधर-सं-हिता, f., N. of a medical work. —शार्ङ्ग-पाणि, इस्, m. ‘bow-handed,’ N. of Viṣṇu; of the father of Viṣṇu; of a chief of the Vaiṣṇava sect. —शार्ङ्ग-भृत्, त्, m. ‘carrying the bow Śārṅga,’ epithet of Viṣṇu.

शार्ङ्गिन्: शार्ङ्गिन्, ई, m. a bowman, an archer; epithet of Viṣṇu; of Śiva.
शार्ङ्गरव: शार्ङ्गरव शार्ङ्गरव, अस्, m. (fr. शृङ्ग-रव?), a Śārṅgarava man, see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 73; (ई), f. a Śāṅgarava woman.
शार्ङ्गष्ठा: शार्ङ्गष्ठा शार्ङ्गष्ठा, f. a kind of tree (= महा-करञ्ज; also written शाङ्गोष्ठा).
शार्दूल: शार्दूल शार्दूल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शॄ), a tiger; a panther or leopard (= चित्रक); any eminent person, best, excellent, pre-eminent (at the end of comps., see व्याघ्र); another kind of animal (= शरभ); a Rākṣasa; a sort of bird; a variety of the Dhṛti metre, (see below); a species of the Atidhṛti metre, (see below); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a Śākhā or school of the Sāma-veda; [cf. perhaps Gr. πάρδος (for κάρδος), πάρδαλις; Lat. pardus, pardalis; Lith. pardas.] —शार्दूल-चर्मन्, अ, n. a tiger's skin. —शार्दूल-मृग-सेवित, अस्, आ, अम्, frequented by tigers and deer. —शार्दूल-ल-लित, अम्, n. ‘tiger's sport,’ a variety of the Dhṛti metre (consisting of four Pādas of eighteen syllables each). —शार्दूल-वाहन, अस्, m. ‘riding on a tiger,’ N. of one of the twenty-five Pūrva-jinas. —शार्दूल-विक्रीडित, अम्, n. ‘tiger's play,’ a species of the Atidhṛti metre (having four Pādas of nineteen syllables each). —शार्दूल-सम-विक्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, having prowess equal to a tiger, as bold as a tiger.

शार्व: शार्व शार्व, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. शर्व), belonging to Śarva or Śiva.
शार्वर: शार्वर शार्वर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शर्वरी), be-longing to night, nocturnal; murderous, mischievous, pernicious; (अम्), n. darkness, gloom; (ई), f. night.
शार्वरिन्: शार्वरिन्, ई, m., N. of the thirty-fourth year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years.
शाल्: शाल् शाल् [cf. rt. शाड्], cl. 1. A. शालते, शालितुम्, to flatter, praise, coax; to boast; to shine or be endowed with [see Malli-nātha's commentary to Kirāt. V. 44].
शाल: शाल शाल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शल् or rt. शाल् or rt. शो; in some senses also written साल, q. v.), a particular tree, the Shorea Robusta or Valeria Robusta (said to be one of the most valuable Indian timber trees, = सर्ज, cf. साल); a tree (in general); an enclosure, court, fence (= प्राकार); a kind of fish, Ophiocephalus Wrahl; N. of a river; of king Śāli-vāhana; (आ), f. a large branch, the upper or main branch of a tree; a hall, saloon, large room, apartment, room; a house; a stable; [cf. Saal, Halle.] —शाल-ग्राम, अस्, m., N. of a sacred place or district; a par-ticular sacred stone worshipped by the Vaiṣṇavas, (it is said to be a kind of black ammonite, and its various circular formations are supposed to have a mystical significance and to be typical of Viṣṇu; these stones are chiefly found in or near the river Gaṇḍakī, and the circles or spirals they contain are thought by some to be formed by the Vajra-kīṭa or other in-sects; cf. साल-ग्राम।) —शालग्राम-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain producing the Śāla-grāma. —शा-लग्राम-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —शाल-ग्राम-शिला, f. the Śāla-grāma stone. —शाल-ज, अस्, m. a kind of fish, (see above.) —शाल-निर्यास, अस्, m. resin, the resinous exudation of the Śāl tree or Shorea Robusta. —शाल-पर्णी, f. ‘having Śāl leaves,’ the shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum, (also written साल-पर्णी।) —शाल-पोत, अस्, m. a young Śāl tree. —शाल-भञ्जिका, f. a doll, wooden puppet; a courtezan, harlot; a kind of game played in the east of India; [cf. साल-भञ्जिका।] —शालभञ्-जिका-प्रख्य, अस्, आ, अम्, resembling the game called Śāla-bhañjikā. —शाल-भञ्जी, f. a doll, wooden puppet (as made of Śāl wood). —शाल-वेष्ट, अस्, m. the resin of the Śāl tree (used as incense &c.), resin (in general). —शाल-सार, अस्, m. a tree; Asa Fetida, (also written साल-सार।) —शालाङ्की (°ला-अङ्°?), f. a doll, puppet. —शालाजिर (°ला-अज्°?), अस्, अम्, m. n. a hollow earthen cup or saucer. —शाला-द्वार, अम्, n. the door or entrance of a hall. —शालाद्वार्य, अस्, m., scil. अग्नि, a kind of sacred or sacrificial fire. —शाला-मृग, अस्, m. ‘house-animal,’ a jackal (as prowling near houses?). —शाला-वती, f., N. of one of the wives of Viśvā-mitra and mother of Hiraṇyākṣa. —शालावत्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family descended from Viśvā-mitra. —शाला-वृक, अस्, m. ‘house-wolf,’ a dog; a cat; a jackal; a wolf; a deer; a monkey; a particular class of evil or malicious beings, (Mahā-bhārata, Śānti-parvan 1188.) —शाला-वृकेय, अस्, m. the offering of a Śālā-vṛka.
शालक: शालक, अस्, m., N. of a man (perhaps a jester in a play).
शालाक्ष: शालाक्ष, आस्, m. pl., N. of a family or Gotra.
शालानी: शालानी, f. the shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum.
शालार: शालार, अम्, n. a ladder, flight of stairs or steps; a bird-cage; the claw of an elephant.
शालिक: शालिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to the Śāl tree; belonging to a hall, &c.; (अस्), m. a weaver; a village of artificers; a toll, tax; (आ), f. the shrub Hedysarum Gangeticum; N. of a Mīmāṃsā work by Śālikā-nātha (= प्रकरण-पञ्चिका)। —शालिका-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Śālikā and of the Praśasta-pāda-bhāṣya-vyākhyāna commentary.

शालिन्: शालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, belonging to a house, domestic, &c.; endowed with, possessed of, possessing, having; shining or resplendent with (generally at the end of comps., cf. वीर्य-श्°; in this sense apparently con-nected with rt. शाल्); (इनी), f. a mistress of a house, housekeeper; a kind of metre, four times ¯¯¯¯¯ ˘¯¯˘¯¯; a proper N. —१। शालि-ता, f. or शालि-त्व, अम्, n. the being endowed with, possession; confidence in.

शाली: शाली, f. a kind of plant (= कृष्ण-जीरक).

P. -करोति, &c., to make humble, humiliate.
शालीय: शालीय, अस्, आ, अम्, of or belonging to a hall; (अस्), m., N. of a Muni.
शालङ्कटङ्कट: शालङ्कटङ्कट शालङ्कटङ्कट, अस्, m., N. of a Rākṣasa (son of Śālaṅkaṭaṅkaṭā, wife of Vidyut-keśin; the N. is also written Śāla-kaṭaṅkaṭa).
शालङ्कायन: शालङ्कायन शालङ्कायन, अस्, m., N. of a Muni; of Śiva's attendant Nandin; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a family (descendants of Viśvā-mitra). —शालङ्का-यन-गोत्र, अम्, n. the family of the Śālaṅkāyanas. —शालङ्कायन-जीवसू, ऊस्, f. epithet of the mother of Vyāsa. —शालङ्कायनी-पुत्र, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher.
शालङ्कायनिन्: शालङ्कायनिन्, इनस्, m. pl., N. of a school.
शालङ्कि: शालङ्कि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
शालञ्च: शालञ्च शालञ्च, अस्, m. = शालाञ्चि below.
शालाक: शालाक शालाक (fr. शलाका), Ved. a frag-ment or splinter of wood, a chip.
शालाकिन्: शालाकिन्, ई, m. a spearman, one armed with a javelin or dart; a surgeon; a barber.

शालाञ्चि: शालाञ्चि शालाञ्चि, इस्, f. = शालिञ्च, p. 1003.
शालातुरीय: शालातुरीय शालातुरीय, अस्, m. (fr. शलातुर), epithet of Pāṇini.
शालालुक: शालालुक शालालुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शलालु), purchased with the perfume called Śalālu.
शालि: शालि शालि, इस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शाल् or fr. rt. शॄ, cf. Uṇādi-s. IV. 127), rice (of which there are said to be ten varieties; but especially two kinds, one white, growing in deep water, and the other red, requiring only a moist soil); the civet-cat, pole-cat; N. of a Yakṣa transformed into a lion, (see शालि-वाहन); (अयस्), m. pl. grains of rice, rice. —शालि-कण, अम्, n. a grain of rice. —शालि-चूर्ण, अस्, अम्, m. n. rice-flower, ground rice. —२। शालि-ता, f. or शालि-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of rice. —शालि-पर्णी, f. a kind of leguminous shrub (= माष-पर्णी). —शालि-पिष्ट, अम्, n. ‘flour of rice,’ crystal. —शालि-भवन, अम्, n. a rice field. —शालि-वाह्, वाट्, -ल्यूही, वाट्, see Vopa-deva IV. 12. —शालि-वाह, अस्, m. a proper N. —शालि-वा-हन, अस्, m., N. of a celebrated sovereign of India (said to be so called either from having in his infancy ridden on a Yakṣa called Śāli, or from Śāli for Śāla, the Śāl tree, Śāli-vāhana being represented as borne on a cross made of that or other wood; he was the enemy of Vikramāditya and institutor of the era now called Śāka, commencing from his birth, seventy-eight years after Christ; his capital was Prati-ṣṭhāna on the Godāvarī). —शालि-शूक, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Maurya dynasty (a descendant of Candra-gupta). —शालि-होत्र, अस्, m. ‘receiving oblations of rice or corn,’ a horse; N. of a writer on veterinary subjects. —शालिहोत्र-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, knowing (the precepts of) Śāli-hotra, skilled in veterinary surgery. —शालि-होत्रिन्, ई, m. a horse. —शाल्य्-ओदन, अस्, अम्, m. n. rice-gruel.
शालेय: शालेय, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, fit for rice (as a field &c.); sown with rice; (अस्, आ), m. f. a sort of fennel, Anethum Panmori or Sowa, = मिश्रेया; (अम्), n. a field of rice.
शालिञ्च: शालिञ्च शालिञ्च, अस्, m. the creeper Achy-ranthes Triandra (the leaves of which are used as a vegetable).

शालु: शालु शालु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. 1. 5. fr. rt. शॄ, but in some senses connected with rt. शल्), a kind of astringent substance; a sort of perfume (commonly called Chor); a frog [cf. शा-लुर]; (उ), n. the root of the water-lily.
शालुक: शालुक, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 42. fr. rt. शल्), the esculent root of the different kinds of Nymphæa or water-lily.
शालुड: शालुड, अस्, m., Ved. a frog.
शालूक: शालूक, अस्, m. a frog; the root of the water-lily (generally neut.); (अम्), n. the root of the water-lily, (see above); the nutmeg (= जाती-फल).
शालोत्तरीय: शालोत्तरीय शालोत्तरीय, अस्, m. (for शाला-तुरीय, q. v.?), N. of the grammarian Pāṇini, (this word is given by Śabda-k. on the authority of the Trikāṇḍa-śeṣa; it is said to be derived from शाला + उत्तरीय, and to account for this derivation a legend is told that Pāṇini was expelled from the house of his preceptor for his stupidity, and acquired his subsequent scholarship by propitiating Śiva.)
शाल्मल: शाल्मल शाल्मल, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. शल् or शाल्), the silk-cotton tree; the gum or resin of the cotton tree (= मोच-रस); one of the Dvīpas or divisions of the continent (= शाल्मलि below). —शालमल-द्वीप, अस्, m. the Śālmala-dvīpa.

शामलिक: शामलिक, अस्, m. the tree Andersonia Rohitaka; (अम्), n. an inferior kind of Śālmali tree.
शाल्मलिन्: शाल्मलिन्, ई, m., N. of Garuḍa, the bird and vehicle of Viṣṇu; (इनी), f. the silk-cotton tree.

शाल्व: शाल्व शाल्व, अस्, m., N. of a country, (also written साल्व, q. v.); a king of the Śālvas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a tribe (inhabiting Bhārata-varṣa). —शाल्व-पति, इस्, or शाल्व-राज, अस्, or शाल्व-राजन्, आ, m. the king of the Śālvas.
शाल्वण: शाल्वण, अस्, m., N. of a class of herbs (used medicinally for expelling wind).
शाल्वेय: शाल्वेय, आस्, m. pl. the inhabitants of Śalva.

शावक: शावक, अस्, m. the young of any animal.
शावसायन: शावसायन, अस्, m. a proper N.

शाश्वतिक: शाश्वतिक, अस्, ई, अम्, eternal, constant, per-petual, permanent.

शाष्कुल: शाष्कुल शाष्कुल, अस्, ई, अम् (said to be an anom. form for शौष्कल fr. शुष्कल), eating flesh or fish.
शाष्कुलिक: शाष्कुलिक शाष्कुलिक, अम्, n. (fr. शष्-कुली), a quantity of baked cakes or pastry.
शास्: शास् 1. शास् (connected with rt. शंस्), cl. 2. P. शास्ति (Ved. and ep. also A. शास्ते; ep. also cl. 1. P. शासति; in some forms शास् is changed to शिस् and this again to शिष्, e. g. Pres. P. 1st du. शिष्वस्, 2nd du. शिष्ठस्, 3rd pl. शासति, Impf. 2nd and 3rd sing. अशात्, Impv. 2nd sing. शाधि, Ved. शिशाधि), शशास, शासिष्यति, अशिषत्, (Ved. form शास्तन, Ṛg-veda X. 52, 1), शासितुम्, to rule, govern, command, order, direct, control; to enact, decree; to train, instruct, inform, teach (with two acc.); to report, proclaim [cf. rt. शंस्]; to correct, punish, chide; (Ved. A.) to implore, wish, desire [cf. आ-शास्, आ-शंस्]; Pass. शिष्यते, to be taught; to learn [cf. शिष्यते under rt. 2. शिष्]: Caus. शासयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशशासत्, to correct, punish: Desid. शिशासिषति: Intens. शेशिष्यते, शाशास्ति।
2. शास्, आस्, m. (connected with rt. शंस्), Ved. one who recites, a reciter, repeater [cf. उक्थ-शास्]; a worshipper.
शास: शास, अस्, m., Ved. order, command, (Sāy. = शा-सन, Ṛg-veda I. 68, 5); praise, hymn of praise, (Sāy. = स्तुति; in this sense connected with rt. शंस्); N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (having the patronymic Bhāra-dhvāja, and author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 152); epithet of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 152.
शास शास, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. शस्), Ved. ‘destroyer,’ epithet of Indra.
शासक: शासक, अस्, इका, अम्, a ruler, governor; a chastiser.
शासत्: शासत्, अत्, अती, अत् (the nom. m. follows the rule for cl. 3), ruling, regulating, governing, commanding.
शासन: शासन, अस्, ई, अम्, one who instructs, instructing, directing, &c.; (ई), f., Ved. an instructress; (अम्), n. the act of governing, ruling, government; an order, edict, enactment, decree, command, direction; the act of instructing, instruction, discipline; a pre-cept; a royal grant, charter (usually a grant of land or of particular privileges, and frequently inscribed on stone or copper); a writing, deed, written contract or agreement; any written book or work of authority, scripture; the control or government of the passions, self-control, devotion. —शासन-दूषक, अस्, इका, अम्, disobeying the command of a king. —शासन-पत्त्र, अम्, n. ‘edict-plate,’ a plate of copper or of stone on which an edict or grant is inscribed; a sheet of paper on which an order is written. —शासन-हर, अस्, m. a command-bearer, one bearing an edict, a royal messenger. —शासन-हारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, bearing commands; (ई), m. a messenger, envoy. —शासनातिवृत्ति (°न-अत्°), इस्, f. the transgression of a command.
शासनीय: शासनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be governed or directed; to be corrected, deserving punishment, punishable.
शासित: शासित, अस्, आ, अम्, governed, ruled, directed; corrected, punished.
शासितव्य: शासितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be governed; to be ordered; to be corrected.
शासितृ: शासितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, ruling, governing; ordering, commanding; one who rules or governs, a governor, commander.
शासिन्: शासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, ruling, directing, controlling; correcting.
शासु: शासु, उस्, m., Ved. a governor, ruler [cf. शास्तृ]; a command, (Sāy. = शासनम्।)
शास्ति: शास्ति, इस्, f. governing, ruling, ordering; a com-mand, order; correction, punishment; a punishment inflicted by royal command; a sceptre.
शास्तृ: शास्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who rules or governs or corrects; a ruler, governor, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda. I. 60, 2. शासुः = शासितुः, gen. c. ‘of a ruler’); teaching, in-structing; (ता), m. a ruler, governor, king; a father; a teacher, master, instructor; a Buddha or Jina or the deified teacher of either of these sects. —शास्तृ-त्व, अम्, n. the state of a ruler, &c.; governing, chastising.
शास्त्र: शास्त्र, अम्, n. ‘an instrument of directing or teaching,’ an order, command, rule, precept, institute; religious or scientific treatise, any sacred book or composition of divine or standard authority (applica-ble even to the Veda, and said to be of fourteen or even eighteen kinds, see under विद्या; the word शास्त्र is often found at the end of a comp. after the word denoting the subject of the book, or applied collectively to whole departments of knowledge, e. g. वेदान्त-श्°, a work on the Vedānta philosophy or the whole body of teaching on that subject; धर्म-श्°, a law-book or whole body of written laws; काव्य-श्°, a poetical work or poetry in general; शिल्पि-श्°, works on the mechanical arts; काम-श्°, erotic compositions; अलङ्कार-श्°, rhetoric, &c.); a book, treatise, body of teaching (in general), scripture, science. —शास्त्र-कृत्, त्, m. the author of a Śāstra; a writer or author (in general); a Ṛṣi or sage (as the author of sacred works). —शास्-त्र-कोविद, अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in sacred works. —शास्त्र-गण्ड, अस्, m. a superficial reader of books; a general reader (= प्रघटा-विद्). —शास्-त्र-चक्षुस्, उस्, n. ‘the eye of science,’ grammer. —शास्त्र-चारण, अस्, आ, अम्, skilled in the Śāstras, well-versed in sacred works or sciences. —शास्त्र-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, knowing sacred works, acquainted with the Śāstras; knowing books; a mere theorist. —शास्त्रज्ञ-ता, f. or शास्त्रज्ञ-त्व, अम्, n. know-ledge of sacred works, acquaintance with the Śāstras. —शास्त्र-ज्ञान, अम्, n. knowledge of sacred works, knowledge derived from the study of the Śāstras. —शास्त्र-तत्त्व, अम्, n. the truth (taught) in sacred works, the truth of the Śāstras. —शास्त्रतत्त्व-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, understanding the truth (as taught in) sacred works; (अस्), m. an astronomer, astrologer. —शास्त्र-तस्, ind. according to the Śāstras, accord-ing to sacred precept or law. —शास्त्र-दर्शिन्, ई, इनी, इ, seeing or knowing the Śāstras, skilled in sacred works or sciences. —शास्त्र-दीपिका, f., N. of a commentary on the Nyāya-sūtras by Pārtha-sārathi. —शास्त्र-दृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, seen in the Śāstras, stated in sacred works or in books treating of any science. —शास्त्र-निन्दा, f. reviling or denying the authority of sacred works. —शास्त्र-प्रसङ्ग, अस्, m. the subject of the Śāstras; the discussion of sacred works. —शास्त्र-योनि, इस्, m. the source of the Śāstras. —शास्त्रयोनि-त्व, अम्, n. the state of being the source of the Śāstras. —शास्त्र-वक्तृ, ता, m. one who expounds sacred books. —१। शास्त्र-वत्, ind. like the sacred writings, conformably or according to written authority. —२। शास्त्र-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having or following sacred institutes, skilled in sacred writings. —शास्त्र-विद्, त्, त्, त्, knowing the Śāstras, understanding or conversant with the scriptures, skilled in sacred sciences. —शास्त्र-वि-धान, अम्, n. or शास्त्र-विधि, इस्, m. scripture-precept, sacred ritual, ceremonial injunction. —शास्-त्रविधानोक्त (°न-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, prescribed by scriptural precept or sacred injunction. —शास्त्र-विप्रतिषिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, forbidden by the Śās-tras, contrary to the scriptures, illegal. —शास्त्र-वि-प्रतिषेध, अस्, m. opposition to the Śāstras, any act contrary to sacred precept or scriptural injunction. —शास्त्र-विमुख, अस्, ई, अम्, disinclined to learn-ing, averse from study. —शास्त्र-विरुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, opposed to the Śāstras, contrary to law or reli-gious precept. —शास्त्र-विरोध, अस्, m. opposition to sacred precept; mutual contradiction of books, incompatibility of different works. —शास्त्र-व्युत्-पत्ति, इस्, f. perfect conversancy with sacred writings. —शास्त्र-शिल्पिन्, ई, m. the country of Kaśmīra; (इनस्), m. pl. the people of Kaśmīra (commonly called Cashmere). —शास्त्र-सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, established by the Śāstras, proved by sacred works. —शास्त्राचरण (°र-आच्°), अम्, n. the study of the Śāstras; (अस्), m. one versed in the scriptures or well read in sacred works; a student of the Vedas or one whose conduct is regulated by their precepts; a Pandit. —शास्त्रातिक्रम (°र-अत्°), अस्, m. trans-gressing the Śāstras, violation of sacred precepts. —शास्त्राननुष्ठान (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. non-performance of sacred precept, disregard of the authority of religious books. —शास्त्रानुष्ठान (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. observance of the Śāstras, con-forming to sacred law or ritual; applying one's self to books. —शास्त्रानुष्ठित (°र-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, established or authorized by the Śāstras, obeying or following sacred institutes. —शास्त्रानुसार (°र-अन्°), अस्, m. conformity to the Śāstras, following sacred ordinances. —शास्त्राभिज्ञ (°र-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, learned in sacred works, versed in the Śās-tras. —शास्त्रार्थ (°र-अर्°), अस्, m. the object or purport of a book, the meaning of a sacred precept, a precept or direction of the Śāstras or of any parti-cular Śāstra, a scriptural statement or dogma. —शास्-त्रोक्त (°र-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, declared or enjoined by the Śāstras, declared in works of sacred authority, said in a book.
शास्त्रित: शास्त्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, treated according to the Śāstras. —शास्त्रितार्थ (°त-अर्°), अस्, m. a scien-tifically treated subject.
शास्त्रिन्: शास्त्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, having or following sacred works, versed in the Śāstras, skilled in books; (ई), m. a teacher of sacred science; a learned man, one who has studied the Śāstras.
शास्त्रीय: शास्त्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, scriptural, authorized by or conformable to sacred precept, agreeable to sacred institutes, legal.
शास्य: शास्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be governed or regulated, to be ordained or prescribed by law; to be corrected; punishable, deserving chastisement or punishment, corrigible.
शिष्ट: शिष्ट, शिष्य, &c. See under 2. शिष्ट, p. 1009.
1. शिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, left, remaining, residual, anything that remains or is left. —१। शिष्ट-ता, f. or शिष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. the being left, the being residual.

शिष्ट 2. शिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. शास्), ordered, commanded; disciplined, well regulated, educated, trained; tamed, obedient, docile; orderly, correct, learned, wise, good; select, (perhaps refer-rible to 1. शिष्ट); eminent, excellent, superior, prin-cipal, chief; (अस्), m. a chief; a courtier, counsellor.  — 2. शिष्ट-ता, f. or शिष्ट-त्व, अम्, n. docility; good behaviour, urbanity, civility. —शिष्ट-सभा, f. an assembly of chiefs, council of state. —शिष्ट-सभाचार (°भा-आच्°), अस्, m. history or tradition of eminent persons. —शिष्ट-सम्मत, अस्, आ, अम्, approved or loved by the learned, (Manu III. 39.) —शिष्टाचरण (°ट-आच्°), अम्, n. the conduct or procedure of the virtuous, practice of the good, gen-tlemanly behaviour. —शिष्टाचार (°ट-आच्°), अस्, m. the practice or traditional usages of the virtuous; (अस्, आ, अम्), well-behaved; the approved conduct of the wise and good, good manners, gentlemanly conduct, proper behaviour. —शिष्टाचार-विरुद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, opposed to the practice of the virtuous. —शिष्टा-चाराविरुद्ध (°र-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, not opposed to the practice of the virtuous.
शाह: शाह शाह, N. of a country (belonging to Kaśmīra).
शाहि: शाहि, इस्, m., N. of a dynasty.
शि: शि 1. शि (closely connected with rt. शो), cl. 5. P. A. शिनोति, शिनुते (Ved. also cl. 3. A. शिशीते), शिशाय, शिश्ये, शेष्यति, -ते, अशैषीत्, अशेष्ट, शेतुम्, to sharpen, whet; to make sharp or thin, attenuate; to excite; to be sharp; to be attentive: Caus. शाययति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशीशयत्: Desid. शिशीषति, -ते: Intens. शेशीयते, शेशयीति, शेशेति; [cf. Gr. κί-ω, κί-νυ-μαι, κἰνέ-ω; Lat. ci-o, ci-e-o, ci-tu-s, excito, incito; Lith. koja.]
2. शि, इस्, m. an epithet of Śiva; auspiciousness, good fortune; peace, composure, calm.
शि 3. शि, (in grammar) a technical term for the case-ending इ, substituted for जस् and शस् in neuters.
शित: शित, अस्, आ, अम् [cf. शात, fr. rt. शो], sharpened, whetted; attenuated, thin, emaciated, wasted, de-clined; weak, feeble. —शित-ता, f. or शित-त्व, अम्, n. sharpness. —शित-धार, अस्, आ, अम्, sharp-edged. —शित-शर, अस्, m. a sharp arrow. —शित-शरा-भीत (°र-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, surrounded or encom-passed with sharp arrows. —शित-सूक, अस्, m. ‘sharp-bearded,’ barley; wheat. —शिताग्र (°त-अग्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sharp-pointed; (अस्), m. a thorn. —शितास्त्र-भृत् (°त-अस्°), त्, m. bearing sharp weapons. —शितेषु (°त-इषु), उस्, m. a sharp arrow. —शितोदा, f. = शीतोदा।
शित शित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. शि or rt. शो), sharpened, &c. See under rt. 1. शि।
शित, अस्, आ, अम्। See under rt. 1. शि।
शित्वा: शित्वा, ind. having sharpened, having whetted.
शिशान: शिशान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. sharpening, making sharp, (Sāy. = तीक्ष्णी-कुर्वत्।)
शिशान शिशान। See under rt. 1. शि, p. 1004.
शिंशपा: शिंशपा शिंशपा or (according to some) शिंशिपा, f. the tree Dalbergia Sisu; the Aśoka tree.
शिंशुमार: शिंशुमार शिंशुमार, अस्, m., Ved. a por-poise (= शिशु-मार).
शिंह्: शिंह् शिंह् = rt. शिङ्घ्, q. v.
शिक्कु: शिक्कु शिक्कु, उस्, उस्, उ, idle, lazy, following no business or profession.
शिक्थ: शिक्थ शिक्थ or शिक्थक, अम्, n. bee's wax, (also written सिक्थक, q. v.)
शिक्य: शिक्य शिक्य, अम्, आ, n. f. (according to Uṇādi-s. V. 16. fr. शि substituted for rt. स्रंस्, cf. शिच्), a kind of loop or swing made of rope and suspended from either end of a pole or yoke to receive a load; the burden or load so carried; a sort of hanging-shelf suspended by strings; the strings of a balance. —शिक्याधार (°या-आध्°), अस्, m. ‘loop-holder,’ the hook or eye at each end of a pole or beam for holding the above looped cord or for hold-ing the strings of a balance.
शिक्यित: शिक्यित, अस्, आ, अम्, placed or carried in the above loop, suspended in a swing or loop made of cord, &c.
शिक्वन्: शिक्वन् शिक्वन् (perhaps connected with शिक्य above), Ved. a rope, cord, (Sāy. शिक्वभिः = रज्जुभिः, Ṛg-veda I. 141, 8.)
शिक्वस्: शिक्वस् शिक्वस् (connected with rt. 1. शक्), Ved. mighty, powerful, able, (Sāy. शिक्वसः = शक्-ताः, Ṛg-veda V. 52, 16; शिक्वसे = शक्ताय, Ṛg-veda X. 92, 9.)
शिक्ष्: शिक्ष् शिक्ष् (properly Desid. of rt. 1. शक्, q. v., but regarded by some as a separate rt.), cl. 1. A. शिक्षते, Aor. अशिक्षिष्ट, शिक्षितुम्, to learn, acquire knowledge; to teach (Ved.); to give (P., Ved., see rt. 1. शक्): Pass. शिक्ष्यते, Aor. अशिक्षि: Caus. शिक्षयति, -ते, Aor. अशिशिक्षत्, -त, to teach, &c., (see rt. 1. शक्, p. 985.)
शिक्षक: शिक्षक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, a learner; a teacher, instructor, (in this sense fr. Caus.); one who knows Śikṣā or the science of euphony, (see below.)
शिक्षण: शिक्षण, अम्, n. the act of learning, acquiring knowledge; teaching, instruction (fr. Caus.).
शिक्षणीय: शिक्षणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be learnt; to be taught (fr. Caus.).
शिक्षत्: शिक्षत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. teaching, instructing.
शिक्षमाण: शिक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. learning; (अस्), m. a learner, pupil.
शिक्षयितृ: शिक्षयितृ, ता, m. (fr. Caus.), an instructor, teacher.
शिक्षयित्वा: शिक्षयित्वा, ind. having taught, having instructed.
शिक्षा: शिक्षा, f. desire of being able to effect anything, wish to prevail (Kirāt. XV. 37); learning, study, the acquisition of knowledge; teaching, instruction, training, discipline; the science which teaches proper pronunciation and especially the laws of euphony peculiar to the Veda, (one of the six Vedāṅgas; see वेदाङ्ग); modesty, humility, diffidence; giving, bestowing (Ved., see rt. 1. शक्); the plant Bignonia Indica. —शिक्षा-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, instruction-caus-ing, instruction-giving; (अस्), m. a teacher, instructor; epithet of Vyāsa. —शिक्षा-गुरु, उस्, m. a religious preceptor, teacher. —शिक्षा-नर, अस्, m., Ved. the chief or foremost in liberality; epithet of Indra, (Sāy. = दानस्य नेता।) —शिक्षा-शक्ति, इस्, f. ‘power of learning,’ dexterity, skill. —शिक्षा-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a section in the Kātantra treating of the pronunciation of letters.
शिक्षाण: शिक्षाण, अस्, आ, अम्, learning, acquiring knowledge.
शिक्षितव्य: शिक्षितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be learnt; to be in-structed or taught.
शिक्षित्वा: शिक्षित्वा, ind. having learnt; having instructed.
शिक्षिन्: शिक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, learning; instructing.
शिक्षु: शिक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of learning, one who wishes to learn.

शिव: शिव शिव, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 153. fr. rt. 1. शी; more probably to be connected with rt. श्वि and शवस्, see शिश्वि), auspicious, pro-pitious, prosperous, happy, fortunate, lucky, increas-ing, thriving, right; (अस्), m., N. of the third god of the Hindū Tri-mūrti, (in the later mythology regarded as ‘the destroyer,’ and with Brahmā, ‘the creator,’ and Viṣṇu, ‘the preserver,’ constituting the well known Hindū triad of divine manifestations; although the name Śiva is not found applied to any god in the Veda, the worship of the destroying and reproducing principle under this name was rapidly developed in the Purāṇas and epic poems, and be-came very general in later times, the worshippers of Śiva or Śaivas assigning to him the first place in the triad and by identifying him with the principles of creation and reproduction as well as that of destruc-tion, constituting him the one Supreme Being who is supposed to comprehend all the powers and forces of nature and whose formidable character makes him the first object of propitiation and adoration; in the Śiva-Purāṇa he is addressed as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, Varuṇa, the Sun, Moon, Earth, Fire, Water, Air, Ether, &c., while even in the Viṣṇu and other Purāṇas not specially devoted to his praise, he is mentioned with the greatest reverence and awe; according to one view the name Śiva belonged originally to the principal god of the aboriginal tribes of India, and being subsequently adopted together with the Liṅga or symbol of reproduction into the Pantheon of the Āryans, was then identified with their own deity Rudra, who occupies a con-spicuous position in the Veda as god of storms; but according to a more likely supposition the adjective शिव, ‘auspicious,’ being at first only used as an euphemistic epithet to propitiate the lord of tempests, passed afterwards into his name, and was ultimately adopted as the principal name of the god of destruc-tion, [see रुद्र]; according to Viṣṇu-Purāṇa I. 8. there are eight principal manifestations of Śiva, viz. Rudra, Bhava, Śarva, Iśāna, Paśu-pati, Bhīma, Ugra, Mahā-deva, which again are visibly represented under eight Tanus or material forms, viz. the Sun, Water, Earth, Air, Fire, Ether, the officiating Brahman, and the Moon, Śiva being supposed to uphold the universe by means of these forms; as presiding over reproduction, which follows destruction, his symbol is the Liṅga or Phallus, under which form he is generally worshipped at the present day; as god of justice or punishment, which character he shares with the gods Yama and Varuṇa, he is represented as riding on a white bull, the god Dharma, it is said, having taken this form and requested Śiva to accept him as his vehicle; his own colour is sometimes depicted as black in his character of destroyer of the world, when he is called Kāla or Time; again, one of his representations is as Ardha-nārī, ‘half-female,’ the other half being male to symbolize the unity of the generative principle, his name being then Ardha-nārīśa, ‘the half-female lord;’ he has sometimes five faces, whence his name Pāñcānana; he has also three eyes, one of which is in his forehead, and which are thought to denote his view of the three divisions of time, past, present, and future, while a moon's crescent, round or above the central eye, marks the measure of time by months, a serpent round his neck the measure of time by years, and a second necklace of skulls with numerous other serpents about his person, the perpetual revolution of ages, and the successive extinction and generation of the races of mankind: his hair is thickly matted together, and gathered above his forehead into a coil, so as to project like a horn; on the top of it he bears the Ganges, the rush of which river in its descent form heaven he intercepted by his head that the earth might not be crushed by the weight of the falling stream; his throat is dark-blue from the stain of the deadly poison which would have destroyed the world had it not been swallowed by him on its production at the churning of the ocean by the gods for the nectar of immortality: he is sometimes represented clothed in a deer-skin, sometimes in a tiger-skin, or he appears sitting on a tiger-skin or holding a deer in one of his hands; in explanation of this a legend is told that Śiva, having once visited a forest in the form of a religious mendicant, the wives of the Ṛṣis residing there fell in love with his great beauty, which the Ṛṣis perceiving resented; in order, therefore, to overpower him, they first dug a pit, and by magical arts caused a tiger to rush out of it, which he slew, and taking its skin wore it as a garment; they next caused a deer to spring out upon him, which he took up in his left hand and ever afterwards retained there; they then produced a red-hot iron, but this too he took up and kept in his hand as a weapon: sometimes, again, he appears wearing an elephant's skin which belonged to an Asura named Gaya, who acquired such power that he conquered the gods and would have destroyed the Munis had they not fled to Benares and taken refuge in a temple of Śiva, who then destroyed the Asura and, ripping up his body, stripped off the hide which he afterwards cast over his shoulders for a cloak: Śiva holds a त्रिशूल or three-pronged trident [also called Pināka] in his hand to denote, as some think, his combination of the three attributes of Creator, Destroyer, and Regenerator; his other weapons are a bow called Ajakava or Ajagava, a thunderbolt, an axe, a kind of staff with transverse pieces surmounted by a skull called Khaṭvāṅga, and another nondescript weapon called Khiṅkira; he also carries a kind of rattle or drum, shaped like an hour-glass, called Ḍamaru, and a Pāśa or noose for binding incorrigible offenders: his attendants or servants are called Pramatha; they are sometimes regarded as demons or supernatural beings of various kinds, and form a complete host; some of his more personal attendants or chamberlains have special names, such as Nandi or Nandin, Bhṛṅgin, Taṇḍu, the latter being the original teacher of dancing &c., whence Śiva is called Naṭeśvara, ‘the lord of dancers,’ and is himself described as नाट्य-प्रिय, fond of dancing: his principal wife Durgā, otherwise called Pārvatī, Umā, Gaurī, Bhavānī, Satī, &c., is the chief object of worship with the Śāktas and Tāntrikas, see शक्ति, शाक्त, तन्त्र: his sons are Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya: he destroyed several Asuras or demons, such as Pura, Tripura, Andhaka, Ruru; he also scorched the god of love, Kāma-deva, to ashes by a glance from his central eye, that deity having attempted to inflame him with passion for Pārvatī whilst he was engaged in severe penance; he is said to have cut off one of the heads of the god Brahmā, that god having ori-ginally possessed five heads, one of which is fabled to have addressed Śiva on a particular occasion in a disrespectful manner, cf. ब्रह्म-मूर्ध-भृत्; he also decapitated Dakṣa and replaced his head by that of a ram, because that sage, who was his father-in-law, omitted to invite him and his wife Satī to a great sacrifice at which all the other gods were present, see दक्षाध्वर-ध्वंश-कृत्; in the exercise of his function of Universal Destroyer he destroys, at the end of every Kalpa, not only all created beings, but even Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the other gods, whose bones and skulls he wears as gar-lands; moreover, at the end of one of the early Kalpas he is fabled to have burnt them up by a flash from his central eye, and afterwards to have rubbed their ashes upon his body, whence the use of ashes is considered of great importance in his worship, while the use of the Rudrākṣa berries or beads originated, it is said, from the legend that Śiva, on his way to destroy the three cities, called Tri-pura, let fall some tears of rage which became converted into these beads: his residence is Kailāsa, one of the loftiest northern peaks of the Himālaya, which is also the paradise of Kuvera: he has strictly no in-carnations like those of Viṣṇu, though Vīra-bhadra and the eight Bhairavas are sometimes regarded as forms of him, sometimes as his sons, see वीर-भ-द्र, भैरव; he is especially worshipped at Be-nares and has even more names than Viṣṇu, one thousand and eight being specified in the sixty-ninth chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa and in the seventeenth chapter of the Anuśāsana-parvan of the Mahā-bhā-rata, some of the most common being Mahā-deva, Śambhu, Śaṅkara, Īśa, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Hara, Rudra); the phallic emblem of Śiva, the male genital organ, penis; a god (= देव, according to Śabda-k.); an auspicious planetary conjunction; the twentieth of the astronomical periods called Yogas, (see योग); शिशयिषु: शिशयिषु, उस्, उस्, उ, wishing to lie down, sleepy, drowsy.
शिशिर: शिशिर शिशिर, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 54. fr. rt. शश्; probably connected with rt. शॄ or rt. शो), cool, chilly, cold, frigid, freezing; (अस्), m., N. of the seventh month of the year (ac-cording to one reckoning); N. of a mountain; of a teacher of the Ṛg-veda (a pupil or descendant of Śā-kalya Veda-mitra); (अस्, अम्), m. n. hoar frost, dew, coolness, cold; the cool or dewy season (comprising two months, Māgha and Phālguna, or from about the middle of January to that of March, see ऋतु). —शिशिर-काल, अस्, m. the dewy season. —शि-शिर-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying frost; (अस्), m. epithet of Agni or fire. —शिशिर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, more cool, very refreshing. —शिशिर-मथित, अस्, आ, अम्, pinched by cold. —शिशिरर्तु (°र-ऋतु), उस्, m. the dewy season. —शिशिरांशु (°र-अं°), उस्, m. ‘having cold rays,’ the moon. —शिशिरांशु-त्व, अम्, n. the state of having cold rays. —शिशिरी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become cool. —शिशिरो-ष्ण-वर्ष (°र-उष्°), आस्, f. pl. the dewy, hot, and rainy seasons.
शिशु: शिशु शिशु, उस्, m. (a reduplicated form of 1. शु for rt. श्वि; according to Uṇādi-s. I. 21. fr. rt. शो; Ved. शिश्वः = शिशवः, शिश्वा = शिशुना), a child, infant; the young of any animal (as a calf, puppy, &c.); a boy under eight years of age; a lad under sixteen; a pupil, scholar; N. of a descendant of Aṅgiras (author of Ṛg-veda IX. 112). —शिशु-काल, अस्, m. childhood. —शिशु-क्रन्द, अस्, m. or शिशु-क्रन्दन, अम्, n. the weeping of a child or infant. —शिशु-क्रन्दीय, अस्, m., scil. ग्रन्थ, a book treating of infantile complaints or (perhaps) a book suitable for naughty children, (Pān. IV. 3, 88.) —शिशु-गन्धा, f. double jasmine. —शिशु-चान्द्रा-यण, अम्, n. the lunar penance of children, (eating four mouthfuls at sunrise and four mouthfuls at sun-set for a month, Manu XI. 219.) —शिशु-त्व, अम्, n. or शिशु-ता, f. childhood, boyhood, the period up to eight years of age; pupilage, the period before sixteen. —शिशु-देश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the place of a child, not far from or almost a child. —शिशु-नाग, अस्, m. a young elephant; a kind of Rākṣasa or demon; N. of a king of Magadhā (the founder of a dynasty). —शिशु-पाल, अस्, m. ‘child-cherisher,’ N. of the king of the Cedis inhabiting a country in central India, probably the same as Bun-delkhand, (see चेदि; he was son of Dama-ghoṣa, and is also called Su-nītha; his impiety in opposing the worship of Kṛṣṇa is described in the Sabhā-parvan of the Mahā-bhārata; when Yudhi-ṣṭhira was about to perform a Rājasūya sacrifice, numerous princes attended, and Bhīṣma proposed that especial honour should be paid to Kṛṣṇa, who was also present, but Śiśu-pāla objected, and after denouncing Kṛṣṇa as a contemptible person challenged him to fight, whereupon Kṛṣṇa struck off his head with his discus; the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa identifies this impious monarch with the demons Hiraṇya-kaśipu and Rā-vaṇa; his death forms the subject of Māgha's cele-brated poem called Śiśupāla-vadha.) —शिशुपालक, अस्, इका, अम्, protecting or cherishing children; (अस्), m., N. of a king (= शिशु-पाल); the plant Nauclea Cordifolia. —शिशुपाल-बध or शिशुपाल-वध, अस्, m. ‘the slaying of Śiśu-pāla,’ N. of a part of the Mahā-bhārata (see below) and of an epic poem by Māgha on the subject of Śiśu-pāla's death by the hand of Kṛṣṇa. —शिशुपाल-बध-पर्वन्, अ, n., N. of a section of the Mahā-bhārata (contained in the Sabhā-parvan 1418 — 1627, see above). —शि-शुपाल-हन्, आ, m. ‘destroyer of Śiśu-pāla,’ an epi-thet of Kṛṣṇa. —शिशु-भाव, अस्, m. the state of childhood, infancy. —शिशु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. infantine, childish, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 140, 10. शिशुमतीर् = शैशववतीर् ज्वालाः।) —शिशु-मार, अस्, m. ‘child-killing,’ the Gangetic porpoise, Delphinus Gangeticus; ‘the heavenly por-poise,’ a form of Viṣṇu (described as a collection of the stars and planets); N. or a form of Viṣṇu. —शिशुमार-शिरस्, अस्, n. the dolphin's head, a part of the heavens studded with stars, the north-east point. —शिशु-वाहक or शिशु-वाह्यक, अस्, m. ‘child-carrier,’ a wild goat. —शिशु-हत्या, f. child-murder.
शिशुक: शिशुक, अस्, m. a child; the young of any animal; a porpoise; a fish resembling a porpoise; a tree.
शिशूल: शिशूल, अस्, m., Ved. a child or a young animal, (Sāy. = शिशु।)
शिश्वन्: शिश्वन् in सं-शिश्वन्, q. v.; (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 65, 5. शिश्वा may either = तनू-कृतः, ‘attenuated,’ as if fr. rt. शो, or = शिशुना, inst. c. of शिशु।)
शिश्वायै: शिश्वायै in Ṛg-veda X. 95, 13 = शिवे, i. e. कल्-याणे समुपस्थिते सति (according to Sāy.).
शिश्वि: शिश्वि, इस्, इस्, इ, swelling, increasing, thriving, &c., in सु-शिश्वि, q. v.
शिश्न: शिश्न शिश्न, अस्, m. (according to Yāska fr. rt. श्नथ्; according to others fr. rt. शश्), the male generative organ, (also अम्, n. in Ved.); (अम्), n., Ved. a tail; thread steeped in rice-water, (said by Sāy. to be fr. rt. स्ना, Ṛg-veda I. 105, 8.) —शिश्न-देव, अस्, m. ‘having the generative organ for a god’ or ‘sporting with that organ,’ a lustful or unchaste man, (Sāy. शिश्नेन दीव्यन्ति क्रीडन्ति इति शिश्न-देवाः अब्रह्मचर्याः इत्य् अर्थः); a tailed or priapic demon. —शिश्नोदर-परायण (°न-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, addicted to lust and gluttony.
शिश्रियाण: शिश्रियाण शिश्रियाण, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्रि), Ved. seeking refuge, taking refuge.
शिश्विदान: शिश्विदान शिश्विदान, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 93. fr. rt. श्वित्, ‘to be white,’ with substitution of द् for त् and elision of the desiderative affix स्), ‘being pure,’ innocent, virtuous (= शुक्ल-कर्मन्); guilty, sinful, wicked (= कृष्ण-कर्-मन् according to some).
शिष्: शिष् 1. शिष्, cl. 1. P. शेषति, शिशेष, शेक्ष्यति, अशिक्षत्, शेष्टुम्, to hurt, injure, kill.

शिष् 2. शिष्, cl. 7. P. शिनष्टि, शिशेष, शेक्ष्यति, अशिषत्, शेष्टुम्, to leave, leave remaining; to distinguish from others, indi-vidualize; (according to some also) cl. 1. P. शेषति, &c., to leave a residue, allow to remain, spare: Pass. शिष्यते, (for शिष्यते, Pass. of rt. 1. शास्, see p. 1003), to be left remaining, remain; Caus. शिष्टि: शिष्टि, इस्, f. ruling, governing, commanding; an order, command; correction, punishment, chastise-ment.
शिष्ट्वा: शिष्ट्वा, ind. having governed or regulated or trained; having ordered or decreed.
शिष्य: शिष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be taught, docile [cf. अ-श्°]; (अस्), m. a scholar, pupil, disciple, (कु-शिष्य, a bad or wicked pupil); passion, anger; violence. —शिष्य-ता, f. or शिष्य-त्व, अम्, n. the state or character of a pupil, pupilage, instruction. —शिष्य-परम्-परा, f. a series or succession of pupils or disciples. —शिष्य-पुत्र, अस्, m. a pupil equal to a son. —शिष्य-प्रदेय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be delivered or imparted to pupils. —शिष्य-शिष्टि, इस्, f. chastise-ment or correction of a pupil.
शिष्यमाण: शिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being ruled or controlled; being instructed or trained.
शिह्ल: शिह्ल शिह्ल or शिह्लक, अस्, m. (also written सिह्ल, q. v.), olibanum, benzoin, Indian incense (= शिला-रस).
शिह्लन: शिह्लन, अस्, m., N. of the author of the Śānti-śataka, (sometimes written शिल्हन।)
शी: शी 1. शी (perhaps connected with rt. शद्), cl. 2. A. शेते (1st du. शेवहे, 3rd du. शयाते, 1st pl. शेमहे, 3rd pl. शेरते, Ved. cl. 1. शयते, but शये = शेते, Ṛg-veda III. 55, 4, cf. Pāṇ. VII. 1, 41; Ved. and ep. also P. in some tenses), Impf. अशेत (P. अशयत्, Ved. 2nd du. P. अशायतम्, 3rd du. Inf. शयध्यै), to lie, lie down, lie on the ground, recline; to rest, repose; to sleep: Pass. शय्यते, Aor. अशायि: Caus. शाययति, -यितुम्, to cause to lie down, put down, throw down; to throw, put; to allow to rest: Desid. शिशयिषते: Intens. शा-शय्यते, शेशयीति, शेशेति; [cf.
