शोत्स्यत्: शोत्स्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to cleanse or purify.
शोद्धव्य: शोद्धव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleansed or purified; to be corrected, &c.
शोध: शोध, अस्, m. purification, cleansing; correction; payment; retaliation. —शोध-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a sheet or paper of corrections; [cf. शुद्धि-प्°।]
शोध शोध, शोधक, शोधन, शोधित, &c. See under rt. शुध्।
शोधक: शोधक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, purificatory, cleans-ing, cleaning, purgative; corrective; (अस्), m. a purifier, refiner; a corrector (in arithmetic or algebra), the subtrahend, the quantity to be subtracted from a number to render it capable of yielding an exact square root; (अम्), n. a particular kind of earth (= कङ्कुष्ठ).
शोधन: शोधन, अस्, ई, अम्, cleaning, purifying, cleansing, refining, purgative; (अम्), n. the act of cleaning, cleansing, purifying, refining; clearance, correction, freeing from faults, clearing away errors, removing or eradicating anything prejudicial or erroneous; precise determination; the cleansing of a sore or wound; the refining of metals, a sort of refining practised for chemical or medicinal purposes, (exposing metals to heat and then sprinkling them with the urine of cows, &c.); payment, clearance or discharge of a debt, quittance, paying off arrears, acquittance; expiation; retaliation, punishment; (in arithmetic) subtraction; excrement, feces, ordure; green vitriol; (अस्), m. the lime (= निम्बूक); a kind of गण्डूष, q. v. (swallowing or rinsing the mouth ?); (ई), f. a broom, brush; a kind of plant (= ताम्र-वल्ली); another plant (= नीली). —शोधनी-वीज, अम्, n. a kind of plant (= जय-पाल).
शोधनक: शोधनक, अस्, m., N. of an officer in an assize court, (Mṛc-chakaṭikā, Act 9.)
शोधनीय: शोधनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be cleansed or purified; to be corrected; to be refined; to be cleared off or discharged; to be paid off or liquidated (as a debt); payable, due; to be subtracted.
शोधयत्: शोधयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, making clean, purifying, cleansing, purging.
शोधयित्वा: शोधयित्वा, ind. having cleared or purified, &c.; having paid or discharged.
शोधित: शोधित, अस्, आ, अम्, cleaned, cleansed; purified, purged; refined; strained, filtered; corrected; ex-cused; cleared off, discharged, paid off, liquidated; acquitted, absolved.
शोधिन्: शोधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, purifying, clearing; requiting, settling.
शोध्य: शोध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be purified or cleansed, to be cleaned or refined; to be cleared off or discharged; payable; due; to be subtracted; (अस्), m. an accused person, one to be cleared or tried; (अम्), n. a con-stant number to be subtracted in some astronomical computations.
शुन्: शुन् शुन्, cl. 6. P. शुनति, &c., to go.
शुन: शुन शुन, अस्, आ, अम् (probably fr. rt. श्वि), white, pure, bright (Ved.; cf. श्वेत); causing pros-perity or happiness, auspicious (Ved.); (अम्), ind. happily, auspiciously (Ved.; Sāy. = सुखम्); (अस्), m., N. of Vāyu (Ved.); a dog, (fr. श्वन्।) —शुन-होत्र, अस्, m., N. of the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda VI. 33, 34 (having the patronymic Bhārad-vāja). —शुनासीरीय or शुनासीर्य, अम्, n. a par-ticular sacrificial oblation (said to be offered in the thirteenth month or Mala-māsa, and probably in honour of Śuna and Sīra). —शुना-सीरौ, m. du., Ved. Śuna and Sīra, N. of two Vedic gods (addressed in Ṛg-veda IV. 57, and identified by Yāska with Vāyu and Āditya; according to other authorities Indra and Vāyu or Indra and Sūrya are meant; but according to another view Sīra may perhaps denote ‘a ploughshare,’ and Śuna some part of a plough). —शुनेषित (°ना-इष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (probably) borne along or carried by dogs.
शुनःपुच्छ: शुनः-पुच्छ, अस्, m. (properly fr. शुनः, gen. c. of श्वन् + पुच्छ), ‘dog-tailed,’ N. of one of the three sons of Ṛcīka (or according to the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa the eldest of the three sons of Ajīgarta); N. of the author of a law-book.
शुनःशेप: शुनः-शेप or शुनः-शेफ, अस्, m. (शुनः, gen. c. of श्वन्), ‘dog-tailed,’ N. of a Vedic Ṛṣi (having the patronymic Ājigarti, as son of Ajigarta or Ajīgarta, and regarded as the author of the hymns Ṛg-veda I. 24-30, IX. 3; according to a legend told in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa VII. 13-18, king Hariścandra, whose priest was Viśvā-mitra, being childless, made a vow that on obtaining a son he would sacrifice him to the god Varuṇa; a son was then born to him named Rohita, but Hariścandra put off on various pretexts the fulfilment of his vow, and when he at length consented to perform it, his son declined being sacrificed, and retiring to the forest passed six years there until he met a poor Brāhman Ṛṣi named Ajīgarta, who had three sons, the second of whom, Śunaḥ-śepha, was purchased by Rohita for a hundred cows to serve as a substitute for himself; Varuṇa having accepted him as a ransom, he was about to be sacrificed, Viśvā-mitra being Hotṛ priest, when he saved himself by reciting verses in praise of various deities, and was received into the family of Viśvā-mitra as one of his sons under the name of Deva-rāta, q. v.: the legend is different in the Rāmāyaṇa, which makes Ambarīṣa, king of Ayodhyā, perform a sacrifice, the victim of which is stolen by Indra; this king is described as wandering over the earth in search of either the real victim or a substitute until he meets with a Brāhman named Ṛcīka, from whom he purchases his middle son, Śunaḥ-śepha, who is about to be sacrificed, when Viśvā-mitra saves him by teaching him a prayer to Agni and two hymns to Indra and Viṣṇu; see Rāmāyaṇa I. 61, 62); (अम्), n. the genital organ of a dog.
शुनक: शुनक, अस्, m. a young dog; a dog; N. of a descendant of Bhṛgu; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a family; [cf. शौनक।] —शुनक-चञ्चुका, f. a kind of plant (= क्षुद्र-चञ्चु). —शुनक-चिल्ली, f. a kind of pot-herb (= श्वान-चिल्लिका). —शुनक-पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of Śunaka, i. e. Śaunaka, (also applied to Gṛtsamada, who is elsewhere described as the father of Śunaka.)
शुनाशीर: शुनाशीर or शुनासीर, अस्, m., N. of Indra, (also written सुनासीर, q. v., cf. शुना-सीरौ under शुन।)
शुनि: शुनि, इस्, m. (fr. श्वन्), a dog.
शुनी: शुनी, f. a female dog, bitch, (see under श्वन्); a kind of gourd (= कुष्माण्डी). —शुनिन्-धम, see Vopa-deva XXVI. 54. —शुनिन्-धय, अस्, ई, अम् (शुनि for शुनी), sucking a bitch, suckled by a bitch.
शुनीर: शुनीर, अस्, m. a number of female dogs.
शुनोलाङ्गूल: शुनो-लाङ्गूल, अस्, m. (fr. शुनः, gen. c. of श्वन् + लाङ्गूल), N. of the youngest of the three sons of Ṛcīka (or of the three sons of Ajīgarta, according to the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa; cf. शुनः-पुच्छ).
शुन्य: 1. शुन्य, अम्, n. (for 2. शुन्य see below), a number of dogs or female dogs.
शुन्य 2. शुन्य, अस्, आ, अम् (more usually written शून्य, q. v.; for 1. शुन्य see p. 1014, col. 3), empty, void; (अम्), n. a cypher.
शुन्ध्: शुन्ध् शुन्ध् (connected with rt. शुध्); cl. 1. P. A. शुन्धति, -ते, शुशुन्ध, शुशुन्धे, शुन्धितुम्, to purify, make clean or pure, cleanse (P., according to some also A.); to be or be-come pure, be purified, be cleansed (A.); cl. 10. P. (according to some also A.) शुन्धयति (-ते), -यि-तुम्, to purify, cleanse.
शुन्धावत्: शुन्धा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (thought by some to be fr. a lost Nom. शुन्ध्य, meaning ‘to desire purifi-cation’), Ved. ‘possessed of desire for purification,’ sacred, holy, pure.
शुन्ध्यु: शुन्ध्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. ‘desirous of purifica-tion,’ purifying; pure, bright; (उस्), m., N. of Agni or fire, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 124, 4, an Āditya or a kind of water-fowl); (उस्), f. a mare, (the chariot of the Sun is said to be drawn by seven mares); [cf. perhaps Lat. castus.]
शुप्: शुप् शुप्, (in grammar) a technical term for the affix उ, the characteristic sign of the eighth class of verbs.
शुफाहिल: शुफाहिल शुफाहिल, N. of a place.
शुभ्: शुभ् 1. शुभ् (perhaps for an original श्वभ्, cf. rts. शुध्, शुम्भ्), cl. 1. A. शोभते (rarely cl. 6. P. शुभति or cl. 1. P. शो-भति, but this latter is referred to rt. 3. शुभ्), शु-शोभ, शुशुभे, शोभिष्यति, -ते, अशुभत्, अशो-भिष्ट, शोभितुम् (Ved. Inf. शोभसे, शुभम्, शुभे, see 2. शुभ्), to shine, be splendid; to be beautiful, look beautiful or handsome, appear to ad-vantage; to be gay or happy; to be victorious, triumph over: Caus. शोभयति, -ते (Ved. also शु-भयति), -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशुभत्, to cause to shine, ornament, decorate: to adorn one's self (A.); to shine (?): Desid. शुशोभिषते, -ति, or शुशुभि-षते, -ति: Intens. शोशुभ्यते, शोशोब्धि, to shine intensely; [cf. Gr. κομψός, κομ-μός, κομέω; Old Germ. sūbar, ‘pure;’ Mod. Germ. sauber; Lith. źibbu.]

2. शुभ्, प्, f., Ved. splendor, beauty, brilliancy, glory; happiness; victory, triumph, (शुभे, for victory or conquest); an ornament; an auspicious offering; a brilliant place of sacrifice, (Sāy. = शो-भन देव-यजन, Ṛg-veda I. 23, 11); water or a brilliant chariot (= उदक or रथ, Ṛg-veda I. 167, 6, &c.). —शुभं-या, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. causing happiness, bestowing blessings, benevolent (said of the wind; Sāy. on Ṛg-veda IV. 3, 6. ex-plains शुभं-ये by शुभस्य प्रापयित्रे, con-necting या with rt. 1. या in the sense of प्रापणे). —शुभं-यावन्, आ, &c., Ved. going to splendor or happiness (said of the Maruts, Sāy. = शोभन-गति, शोभनं गन्ता; cf. ऋण-यावन्). —शु-भस्-पति, इस्, m. lord or preserver of splendor, (Sāy. = शोभनस्य कर्मणः पालकः); (ई), m. du., Ved. epithet of the two Aśvins.
शुभ् 3. शुभ् (sometimes written शुन्भ् or शुम्भ् = rts. सुभ्, सुन्भ्, सुम्भ्), cl. 1. P. शोभति, शुन्भति, &c., to shine [cf. rt. 1. शुभ्]; to speak; to strike, injure, kill.
शुभ: शुभ, अस्, आ, अम्, bright, shining, splendid, hand-some, beautiful; auspicious, fortunate, lucky, happy, well, right, good, virtuous, eminent, distinguished; learned, versed in the Vedas; (अस्), m. the twenty-third of the astronomical Yogas; a city in the sky, (see व्योमचारि-पुर; said to be also fem. and neut.); (आ), f. light, lustre; beauty; desire; N. of a female friend and companion of the goddess Umā; an assembly of the gods; bamboo-manna; white Dūrvā grass; the Śamī tree; the yellow pigment गो-रोचना; a particular plant, = प्रियङ्गु; (अम्), n. anything bright or beautiful, auspiciousness; hap-piness, hail, welfare, good fortune, good; an orna-ment; water, rain, (Sāy. = अलङ्कार or उदक, Ṛg-veda VII. 82, 5); a fragrant wood (= पद्म-काष्ठ); [cf. Pers. خوب khūb.] —शुभ-कर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, causing welfare, producing good, propitious, &c. —शुभ-कर्मन्, अ, n. a good or virtuous act, auspicious action; reputable occupation or employment. —शुभ-कृत्, त्, m. epithet of the thirty-sixth or tenth year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years. —शुभ-क्षण, अस्, अम्, m. n. an auspicious or lucky moment. —शुभ-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, going well or beautifully, graceful, elegant; propitious, for-tunate. —शुभ-गन्धक, अस्, आ, अम्, good-scented; (अम्), n. gum-myrrh. —शुभ-ग्रह, अस्, m. an auspicious planet, lucky star (such as Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and the moon when more than half full). —शुभग्रहोदय (°ह-उद्°), अस्, m. the rising of an auspicious planet. —शुभङ्-कर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, conferring happiness or fortune; auspicious, propitious; (ई), f. Pārvatī. —शुभ-जानि, इस्, इस्, इ, having a beautiful wife. —शुभ-द, अस्, आ, अम्, granting happiness, propitious, auspicious; (अस्), m. the sacred fig-tree (= अश्वत्थ). —शुभ-दन्ती, f. a woman with good teeth; the female elephant of Puṣpa-danta or of the north-west quarter, (also read शुभ्र-दन्ती।) —शुभ-दृष्टि, इस्, f. an auspicious look or aspect. —शुभ-धर, अस्, m. a proper N. —शुभ-नामा, f. epithet of the fifth lunar night. —शुभ-पत्त्रिका, f. ‘having auspicious leaves,’ a kind of shrub (= शाल-पर्णी). —शुभ-फल, अम्, n. auspicious result, good or happy consequence. —शुभम्-भावुक, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘disposed to be bright,’ resplendent, decorated, ornamented. —शुभ-योग, अस्, m. a particular astronomical Yoga, (see शुभ।) —शुभ-लक्षण, अस्, आ, अम्, having an auspicious sign or symptom; marked or charac-terized by felicity. —शुभ-लग्न, अस्, अम्, m. n. the rising of an auspicious constellation, a lucky moment. —शुभ-वार्त्ता, f. good news. —शुभ-वासन, अस्, m. auspicious perfuming; perfume for the mouth. —शुभ-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a particular religious observance (kept on the twelfth day in one of the halves of the month Kārttika). —शुभ-शंसिन्, ई, इनी, इ, indicative of good luck. —शुभ-शील, अस्, आ, अम्, well-disposed, having a good disposition. —शु-भ-संयुत, अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with prosperity or happiness, blissful. —शुभ-सप्तमी-व्रत, अम्, n., N. of a particular religious observance. —शुभ-सूचनी, f. ‘indicating good,’ N. of a female deity worshipped by women in times of calamity, (she is also called Su-vacanī.) —शुभ-स्थली, f. any auspicious place, a room or hall in which sacrifices are offered. —शुभाक्ष (°भ-अक्°), अस्, m. ‘auspicious-eyed,’ epithet of Śiva. —शुभागम (°भ-आग्°), अम्, n. epithet of certain Tantra works regarded as especially orthodox. —शुभाङ्ग (°भ-अङ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, handsome-limbed, beautifully formed, handsome, elegant; (अस्), m., N. of a lexicographer; of another person; (ई), f. a handsome woman; N. of Rati (wife of the god of love); of the wife of Kuvera (god of wealth). —शुभाचार (°भ-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, pure in practices or observances, virtuous; (आ), f. epithet of a female attendant on Umā; [cf. शु-भा।] —शुभाञ्जन (°भ-अञ्°), अस्, m. the tree Hyperanthera Moringa, (see शोभाञ्जन।) —शु-भानन (°भ-आन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, handsome-faced, good-looking; (आ), f. a handsome woman. —शु-भानन्दा (°भ-आन्°), f., N. of a goddess. —शु-भान्वित (°भ-अन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with prosperity or good fortune, happy, prosperous. —शु-भापाङ्गा (°भ-अप्°), f. ‘a woman who has beauti-ful eye-corners,’ a beautiful woman. —शुभाशुभ (°भ-अश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, prosperous and unfortunate, good and evil; (अम्), n. good and evil, good and bad fortune, weal and woe. —शुभाशुभ-लक्-षण, अम्, n. a mark or sign of good or bad fortune, a good or evil omen. —शुभेतर (°भ-इत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, other than auspicious, unlucky, in-auspicious; evil, bad. —शुभोदर्क (°भ-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having prosperous results or happy con-sequences; causing happiness.
शुभंयु: शुभंयु, उस्, उस्, उ, happy, fortunate, pros-perous, auspicious.
शुभान: शुभान, अस्, आ, अम्, shining bright, brilliant; (आस्), m. pl. (according to some) epithet of the Maruts, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 165, 3. शुभानैः = शोभमानैर् वचनैः।)
शुभिका: शुभिका, f., Ved. a garland formed of flowers.
शुभ्र: शुभ्र, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, radiant, bright; white; (अस्), m. white (the colour); sandal; (अम्), n. silver; talc; green vitriol; rock or fossil salt; (आ), f. the Ganges; crystal; bamboo-manna; [cf. Old Germ. sūbar; Mod Germ. sauber, ‘clean;’ Angl. Sax. syfr.] —शुभ्र-कृत्, त्, m. the thirty-sixth year of Jupiter's cycle; [cf. शुभ-कृत्।] —शुभ्र-खादि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. having shining rings, having bright weapons (said of the Maruts; Sāy. = शोभनायुध or शोभन-हविष्क, Ṛg-veda VIII. 20, 4). —शुभ्र-ता, f. or शुभ्र-त्व, अम्, n. whiteness. —शुभ्र-दन्ती, f. the female elephant of Puṣpa-danta, the elephant of the north-west quarter, (see शुभ-दन्ती।) —शुभ्र-रश्मि, इस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon. —शुभ्र-शस्तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining very much, (according to some either for शुभ्र-शस्त-तम or for शुभ्र-शस्-तम।) —शुभ्रांशु (°र-अं°), उस्, m. ‘white-rayed,’ the moon; camphor. —शुभ्रालु (°र-आलु), उस्, m. a white esculent root; a particular plant with a tuberous root (= महिष-कन्द). —शु-भ्रा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessing radiance, shining.
शुभ्रि: शुभ्रि, इस्, इस्, इ, shining bright (Ved., Sāy. = शो-भन); (इस्), m. an epithet of Brahmā.
शोभ: शोभ, अस्, आ, अम्, bright, brilliant, handsome; (आ), f. light, lustre, radiance, splendor, sheen, bril-liancy; beauty, elegance, grace, comeliness; dis-tinguished merit; turmeric; the yellow pigment गो-रोचना; a species of the Kṛti metre. —शोभ-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, causing lustre, beautifying; (त्), m. the thirty-seventh (or sixth) year of Jupiter's cycle of sixty years [cf. शुभ-कृत्]; the marking-nut plant. —शोभा-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing lustre, beautifying. —शोभाञ्जन (°भा-अञ्°), अस्, m. the tree Hyperanthera Moringa (commonly called Śa-jinā; it is much valued for its various properties; the legumes, blossoms, and leaves are esculent; the root of the young tree is used as a substitute for horse-radish as well as a stimulant in medicine, and the expressed oil of the seeds is said to relieve arthritic pains; it has a great many synonyms; cf. शिग्रु, नील-शिग्रु, काक्षीवक, जन-प्रिय, च-क्षुष्य, &c.). —शोभा-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, full of lustre or beauty; beautiful. —शोभा-वती, f., N. of a town.
शोभ शोभ, शोभन, शोभित, &c. See under rt. 1. शुभ्।
शोभथ: शोभथ, Ved. splendor, (used only in the inst. c. शोभथा।)
शोभन: शोभन, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, adorning, causing to look beautiful, shining, splendid; beautiful, hand-some, (sometimes used ironically); richly dressed or ornamented; propitious, auspicious; virtuous, de-corous, good, moral; (अस्), m. a burnt offering for auspicious results; epithet of Śiva; epithet of the eleventh year of Jupiter's cycle; a planet; the fifth of the astronomical Yogas; (आ), f. turmeric; the yellow pigment गो-रोचना; (अम्), n. the act of adorning or causing to look beautiful; the being bright or handsome, brilliance, sheen; a lotus. —शोभन-वाह, अस्, आ, अम्, having splendid car-riers or horses. —शोभनाचरित (°न-आच्°), अम्, n. virtuous practice.
शोभनक: शोभनक, अस्, m. the tree Hyperanthera Mo-ringa (= शोभाञ्जन above).
शोभनीय: शोभनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be beautified or adorned.
शोभमान: शोभमान, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, looking beauti-ful or handsome, splendid, fair.
शोभयत्: शोभयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to shine, orna-menting, decorating.
शोभस्: शोभस्, अस्, n., Ved. splendor, beauty, (the dat. c. शोभसे is used as a Ved. Inf.; Sāy. = शोभनार्-थम्।)
शोभित: शोभित, अस्, आ, अम्, beautiful, adorned, decorated, trimmed, made splendid.
शोभिन्: शोभिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shining, brilliant, beautiful, handsome, distinguished, exceeding.
शोभिष्ठ: शोभिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most brilliant, very handsome or beautiful.
शुम्भ्: शुम्भ् शुम्भ्, cl. 6. P. A. शुम्भति, -ते, शुशुम्भ, शुम्भिष्यति, शुम्-भितुम्, Ved. to shine, be brilliant; to decorate; cl. 1. P. शुम्भति, &c., to shine; to speak; to strike, injure, kill, (in these senses = rts. 3. शुभ्, सुभ्, सुम्भ्): Caus. A., Ved. शुभयते, -यितुम्, to decorate one's self, to shine; [cf. probably Gr. κομψός.]
शुम्भन: शुम्भन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. shining, brilliant.
शुम्भमान: शुम्भमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. decorating, adorn-ing; handsome, beautiful, (Sāy. = शोभमान।)
शुम्भान: शुम्भान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. decorating, illumi-nating, (Sāy. = शोभयत्।)
शुम्भ: शुम्भ शुम्भ, अस्, m., N. of an Asura or demon slain by Durgā, (he was son of Gaveṣṭhin and grandson of Prahlāda.) —शुम्भ-घातिनी or शुम्भ-मर्दिनी, f. ‘Śumbha-killing,’ an epithet of Durgā. —शुम्भ-पुर, अम्, ई, n. f. ‘the city of the Asura Śumbha,’ a town and district, (the modern Sambhalpūr in the district of Gondwāna; it is also called Eka-cakra and Hari-gṛha.) —शुम्-भ-बध or शुम्भ-वध, अस्, m. ‘killing of Śumbha,’ N. of the tenth chapter of the Devī-māhātmya of the Mārkaṇḍeya-Purāṇa.
शुर: शुर शुर, अस्, m. (for शूर, q. v.), a hero; a lion, &c.
शुरुध्: शुरुध् शुरुध्, धस्, f. pl., Ved. gifts, treasures, riches; waters, water, (Sāy. = आपः, Ṛg-veda IV. 23, 8); preventers or alleviators of pain or sorrow, (Sāy. = शुचेर् दुःखस्य प्रतिरोद्धारः or शोकस्य रोधयितृ); herbs or other remedies used to allay pain; exhilarating drinks (according to some).
शुल्क्: शुल्क् शुल्क्, cl. 10. P. शुल्कयति, -यितुम्, to pay, give; to gain, acquire; to abandon, leave, forsake; to create (सर्जने); to narrate, tell; [cf. rt. श्वल्क्।]
शुल्क: शुल्क, अस्, अम्, m. n. toll, tax, duty, customs (especially money levied at ferries, passes, and roads); a sum of money, price, (Sāy. = मूल्य); property, wealth, (Sāy. = धन); gain, profit; money ad-vanced to ratify a bargain; money given to the parents of the bride (originally as purchase-price); a present made by a bridegroom to his bride; nuptial present; a marriage-settlement or dower; a wife's perquisites or private property (such as the profits of household labour, domestic utensils, milch cattle, ornaments, servants, &c.). —शुल्क-खण्डन, अम्, n. defrauding the revenue. —शुल्क-ग्राहक, अस्, इका, अम्, or शुल्क-ग्राहिन्, ई, इणी, इ, receiving a toll or duty. —शुल्क-द, अस्, m. the giver of a nuptial present, an affianced suitor. —शुल्क-मो-षण, अम्, n. stealing or defrauding the revenue. —शुल्क-शाला, f. a custom-house; [cf. शौल्क-शालिक।] —शुल्क-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, having (merely) the name of a nuptial gratuity. —शुल्क-स्थान, अम्, n. a toll-office, custom-house (Manu VIII. 400); any object of taxation or duty. —शुल्क-हानि, इस्, f. loss or forfeiture of wages or dower, &c. —शुल्का-भिधान (°क-अभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, = शुल्क-सञ्ज्ञ। —शुल्कावाप्त (°क-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, obtained as a dowry.
शुल्किक: शुल्किक शुल्किक, अस्, m., N. of a country or district; [cf. शौल्किकेय।]
शुल्ल: शुल्ल शुल्ल, अम्, n. (for शुल्व), a cord, rope, string; copper (= ताम्र; cf. शुल्व).
शुल्व्: शुल्व् शुल्व् (also written शुल्ब्), cl. 10. P. शुल्वयति, -यितुम्, to send away, dis-miss; to measure; to create.
शुल्व: शुल्व or शुल्ब, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. IV. 95. fr. rt. 1. शुच्), a rope, cord, string, (said to be also अस्, m., आ or ई, f.); copper, a copper vessel; a sacrificial observance; institute, law, custom; a quantity of water; (आनि), n. pl., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda; [cf. शुल्विक।] —शुल्व-ज, अम्, n. brass. —शुल्व-दीपिका, f., N. of a work. —शुल्व-परिशिष्ट and शुल्व-वार्त्तिक and शुल्व-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of works. —शुल्वारि (°व-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of copper,’ sulphur.
शुल्विक: शुल्विक, आनि, n. pl., N. of a Pariśiṣṭa of the Yajur-veda.
शुशुक्षणि: शुशुक्षणि शुशुक्षणि in आ-शुशुक्षणि, q. v.
शुशुमा: शुशुमा शुशुमा, f., N. of the wife of Śukra.
शुशुलूकयातु: शुशुलूकयातु शुशुलूक-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a demon in the shape of an owlet, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 22. शुशूलूक = शिशूलूक, a small owl; cf. उलूक-यातु।)
शुश्रुवस्: शुश्रुवस् शुश्रुवस्। See under rt. 1. श्रु।
शुश्रुवस्, आन्, उषी, अत्, one who has heard, &c.
शुश्रू: शुश्रू शुश्रू, ऊस्, f. (fr. Desid. of rt. 1. श्रु), ‘one who waits on a child,’ a mother.
शुश्रूषक: शुश्रूषक, अस्, आ, अम्, desirous of hearing, attentive, obedient, attending or waiting on; (अस्), m. an attendant, servant (comprehending five de-scriptions of persons, viz. a pupil, a religious pupil, a hired servant, an officer, and a slave).
शुश्रूषण: शुश्रूषण, अम्, n. obedience; dutiful homage, close and assiduous attendance, service, serving.
शुश्रूषा: शुश्रूषा, f. desire or wish to hear, desire to obey, obedience; service (said to be of five kinds, see शुश्रूषक); obsequiousness, reverence; say-ing, speaking, telling. —शुश्रूषा-पर, अस्, आ, अम्, diligent or attentive in service.
शुश्रूषित्वा: शुश्रूषित्वा, ind. having attended or waited upon (as a slave upon his master, Manu XI. 110).
शुश्रूषु: शुश्रूषु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of hearing or obey-ing, obedient, attentive, serving, attending.
शुष्: शुष् शुष् (thought to be for सुष्, which again was probably for an original सुस्), cl. 4. P. शुष्यति (ep. also A. -ते), शुशोष, शोक्ष्-यति, अशुषत्, शोष्टुम्, to dry, become dry, dry up; to wither, become withered; to languish, be-come emaciated; to be afflicted: Caus. शोषयति, -ते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशुषत्, to make dry, dry up, wither, parch; to emaciate; to destroy; to extinguish: Desid. शुशुक्षति: Intens. शोशुष्यते, शोशोष्टि; [cf. Zend hushka: Gr. σαυαρός, σαυσαρισμός, σαυκός (= शुष्क), σαυχμός, αὐχμός, σαχνός, αὔω, αὖος, αὐστηρός: Lat. siccus: Goth. siuk, sauht: Old Germ. siuh, siuchi, siuhjan, suht: Angl. Sax. seoc, seac, sioc, sic, suht: Slav. such, ‘dry:’ Lith. sausa-s: Hib. seacadh, ‘parched, frozen;’ sioc, ‘frost;’ sican.]
शुष: शुष, अस्, ई, m. f. drying, drying up; a hole in the ground.
शुषत्: शुषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. drying up, absorbing (moisture).
शुषि: शुषि, इस्, f. drying; a hole, chasm; the hollow or groove in the fang of a snake; [cf. Gr. κυσό-ς, κυσ-θό-ς; Lat. cun-nu-s; Lith. kuszy-s.]
शुषिर: शुषिर, अस्, आ, अम्, full of holes or crevices (caused by drying), perforated, bored, pierced, full of interstices or spaces; (अम्), n. a hole, vacuity, chasm; the atmosphere; a wind-instrument; (अस्), m. fire; a rat, mouse; (आ), f. a river; a sort of per-fume (commonly called Nalī).
शुषिल: शुषिल, अस्, m. ‘the dryer,’ air, wind.
शुष्क: शुष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, dry; shriveled, withered, emaciated, shrunk up; groundless, cause-less; unproductive, fruitless, unprofitable; offensive; (अम्), n., Ved. anything dry, dry wood (for lighting fire by attrition). —शुष्क-कलह, अस्, m. vain or useless wrangling, a quarrel about trifles. —शुष्क-ता, f. or शुष्क-त्व, अम्, n. dryness. —शुष्क-पत्त्र, अम्, n. a dry or withered leaf; a dried pot-herb. —शुष्क-पर्ण, अम्, n. a dry or withered leaf. —शुष्क-फल, अम्, n. dry fruit. —शुष्क-मत्स्य, अस्, m. a dried fish. —शुष्क-मांस, अम्, n. dry flesh, dry meat. —शुष्क-रेवती, f. epithet of a particular Mātrikā or goddess presiding over a kind of disease; [cf. रेवती, पूतना।] —शुष्क-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, dried up. —शुष्क-वृक्ष, अस्, m. a dry tree; a particular plant or shrub (= धव). —शुष्क-वैर, अम्, n. ground-less enmity. —शुष्क-व्रण, अस्, m. a dried up wound, cicatrized sore, scar. —शुष्क-स्रोत, अस्, आ, अम्, having the stream dried up. —शुष्काङ्ग (°क-अङ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, having shriveled limbs, emaciated, withered; (अस्), m. a particular plant or shrub, = धव; (ई), f. a lizard, chameleon. —शुष्कान्न (°क-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘dry food,’ rice in the husk. —शुष्कार्द्र (°क-आर्°), अम्, n. dry ginger.
शुष्कल: शुष्कल, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, m. f. n. dry flesh; flesh; one who eats flesh.
शुष्ण: शुष्ण, अस्, m. the sun; fire; N. of a demon of drought (represented in the Ṛg-veda as being over-come by Indra); (अम्), n., Ved. strength, (enume-rated among the बल-नामानि in Naigh. II. 9.) —शुष्ण-हत्य, अम्, n., Ved. the slaughter of Śuṣṇa.
शुष्म: शुष्म, अस्, आ, अम्, strong, powerful (Ved.); (अस्), m. power, strength, vigour (Ved.); the sun; fire, flame, light; air, wind; a bird; (अम्), n. strength, prowess (= बल, Naigh. II. 9); light, lustre.
शुष्मन्: शुष्मन्, आ, m. fire; a particular plant, = चि-त्रक; (अ), n. light, lustre; strength, prowess.
शुष्मिण: शुष्मिण, अस्, m., N. of a king of the Śivis.
शुष्मिन्: शुष्मिन्, ई, इणी, इ, powerful, strong; fiery, mettle-some; (इणस्), m. pl., N. of a caste living in Kuśa-dvīpa (corresponding to the Kṣatriyas). —शुष्-मिन्-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. most powerful, very mighty.
शुष्यत्: शुष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, becoming dry, drying up.
शुष्यमाण: शुष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being dry or dried up, languishing, thirsty.
शोष: शोष, अस्, m. drying up, exsiccation, dryness; pulmonary consumption; emaciation; intumescence, (for शोथ।) —शोष-सम्भव, अम्, n. the root of long pepper. —शोषापहा (°ष-अप्°), f. ‘re-moving consumption,’ a kind of plant (= क्लीत-नक).
शोष शोष, शोषन, शोषित, &c. See under rt. शुष्।
शोषक: शोषक, अस्, इका, अम्, drying up, exsiccating, absorbing, absorbent.
शोषण: शोषण, अस्, ई, अम्, drying up, draining; causing to fade; (अस्), m. one of the arrows of Kāma-deva (god of love); the plant Bignonia Indica; (अम्), n. the act of drying up; absorption; exhaustion; suck-ing up, suction; dry ginger.
शोषणीय: शोषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up or absorbed.
शोषयितव्य: शोषयितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be dried up, &c.
शोषित: शोषित, अस्, आ, अम्, dried, dried up, desiccated, absorbed, sucked up, exhausted, drained, emptied.
शोषिन्: शोषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, drying up (often at the end of comps.); (इणी), f. ether, one of the five Dhāraṇās.
शूक: शूक शूक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. शो), the awn of barley, &c.; a bristle, spicule; the bristle or sharp hair of insects, &c.; compassion, clemency, tenderness; a kind of venomous insect or lizard (produced in stagnant water); a sort of water-leech (?); a kind of moss or weed growing on stagnant water (= जल-श्°); a particular remedy in which the Śūka is used; (आ), f. cowach. —शूक-कीट or शूक-कीटक, अस्, m. a kind of caterpillar covered with bristles or hairs. —शूक-तृण, अम्, n. a kind of grass. —शूक-धान्य, अम्, n. any awned or bearded grain (as barley &c.). —शूक-पिण्डि, इस्, or शूक-पिण्डी, f. cowach (= कपि-कच्छु). —शूक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, awned, bearded; (अती), f. cowach. —शूक-शिम्बा, f. or शुक-शिम्बि, इस्, or शूक-शिम्बिका or शूक-शिम्बी, f. cowach, (also spelt शुक-शिम्बा, q. v.)
शूकक: शूकक, अस्, m. barley or a bearded kind of wheat resembling barley; the sentiment of compassion or tenderness.
शूकिन्: शूकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, awned, bearded (as corn, grain, &c.).
शूकर: शूकर शूकर, अस्, m. (said to be connected with शूक, or fr. शू, an imitative sound, + कर; cf. सूकर), a hog, pig; N. of a Naraka; (ई), f. a sow; a kind of moss, Lycopodium Imbricatum; [cf. Gr. αῦς, ὗς; Old Germ. sū; Mod. Germ. sau.] —शूकर-कन्द, अस्, m. ‘hog's root,’ a kind of bulbous plant (= वाराही-कन्द). —शूकर-दंष्-ट्र, अस्, m. a hog's tusk; N. of a kind of disease, (prolapsus ani.) —शूकर-पादिका, f. a kind of plant (= कोल-शिम्बी). —शूकराक्रान्ता (°र-आक्°), f. a kind of moss (= वराह-क्रान्ता). —शूकरेष्ट (°र-इष्°), अस्, आ, अम्, liked by hogs or swine; (अस्), m. a kind of grass (= कसेरु).
शूकल: शूकल शूकल, अस्, m. a restive horse; [cf. शूलक।]
शूकापुट्ट: शूकापुट्ट शूकापुट्ट or (according to Śabda-k.) शूकापूट्ट, अस्, m. a particular gem, (perhaps) a kind of amber (= तृण-मणि).
शूकुल: शूकुल शूकुल, अस्, m. (?), a fish in general; a kind of fish; a fragrant grass, Cyperus.
शूकृत: शूकृत शू-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. making the sound शू or शूत्, snorting (said of a horse).
शूक्ष्म: शूक्ष्म शूक्ष्म, incorrect for सूक्ष्म, q. v.
शूघन: शूघन शूघन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. going quickly, (Sāy. शूघनासः = आशु-गन्त्र्यः, Ṛg-veda IV. 58, 7.)
शूतिपर्ण: शूतिपर्ण शूति-पर्ण, अस्, m. (the meaning of शूति is doubtful), a kind of tree (= आरग्-बध).
शूद्र: शूद्र शूद्र, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 19. fr. rt. 1. शुच्, to be afflicted, &c.), a man of the fourth or servile tribe (whose only business, ac-cording to Manu I. 91, was to serve the three higher castes; in Ṛg-veda X. 90, 12. the Śūdra is said to have been born from the feet of Puruṣa; in Manu I. 87. he is fabled to have sprung from the same part of the body of Brahmā; केवल-शूद्र, a pure Śūdra); (आ), f. a woman of the Śūdra tribe; (ई), f. the wife of a Śūdra. —शूद्र-कन्या, f. a Śūdra girl. —शूद्र-कृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be done by a Śūdra, proper for a Śūdra; (अम्), n. the duty of a Śūdra. —शूद्रकृत्य-विचार-तत्त्व, अम्, n., N. of a part of Raghu-nandana's Smṛti-tattva (illustrat-ing the duties of Śūdras at the anniversaries of the death of parents and at other ceremonies). —शूद्र-ता, f. or शूद्र-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a Śūdra or slave; servility. —शूद्र-धर्म, अस्, m. the duty of a Śūdra (i. e. the service of the three higher castes). —शूद्रधर्म-तत्त्व, अम्, n. ‘the nature of a Śūdra's duties,’ N. of a work by Kamalākara. —शूद्र-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, dear to a Śūdra, liked by Śūdras; (अस्), m. an onion (= प-लाण्डु). —शूद्र-प्रेष्य, अस्, m. a man of one of the three superior castes who has become a servant to a Śūdra; (अम्), n. the being servant to a Śūdra. —शूद्र-भिक्षित, अस्, आ, अम्, (anything) begged or received as alms from a Śūdra. —शूद्र-भू-यिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, inhabited mostly by Śūdras, abounding with Śūdras. —शूद्र-याजक, अस्, m. one who sacrifices for a Śūdra, the conductor of a sacrifice for a Śūdra. —शूद्रयाजक-प्रायश्चित्त, अम्, n. the penance incurred by sacrificing for a Śūdra. —शूद्र-योनि-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born of a ser-vile womb, of plebeian origin. —शूद्र-राज्य, अम्, n. a country of which a Śūdra is king. —शूद्र-वर्ग, अस्, m. the Śūdra or servile class. —शूद्र-वर्जम्, ind. except Śūdras. —शूद्र-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the occupation or mode of life of a Śūdra (i. e. ser-vitude to the higher castes). —शूद्र-शासन, अम्, n. an edict or grant addressed to Śūdras. —शूद्र-संस्कार, अस्, m. any purificatory rite relating to Śūdras. —शूद्र-सेवन, अम्, n. attendance on a Śūdra master, the being in the service of a man of the servile class, (Manu XI. 70.) —शूद्र-हत्या, f. the killing of a Śūdra. —शूद्र-हन्, आ, m. one who kills a Śūdra, the slayer of a Śūdra. —शू-द्रान्न (°र-अन्°), अम्, n. food belonging to a Śūdra; [cf. शूद्रोदक below.] —शूद्रा-परिण-यन, अम्, n. the marrying a Śūdra female. —शू-द्रा-पुत्र, अस्, m. the son of a Śūdra woman, (the father being either a Śūdra or a man of a different caste.) —शूद्रा-भार्य, अस्, m. one who has a Śūdra woman for his wife, the husband of a Śūdra woman. —शूद्रार्ता (°र-आर्°), f. a kind of plant (= प्रियङ्गु). —शूद्रा-वेदन, अम्, n. the mar-rying a Śūdra woman. —शूद्रा-वेदिन्, ई, m. marry-ing a Śūdra woman, a man of one of the three higher classes who has married a Śūdra wife. —शू-द्राशौच (°र-अश्°), अम्, n. the impurity of a Śūdra. —शूद्रा-सुत, अस्, m. = शूद्रा-पुत्र. —शू-द्राह्निक (°र-आह्°), अम्, n. the daily ceremonies of a Śūdra. —शूद्री-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become a Śūdra. —शूद्रोदक (°र-उद्°), अम्, n. water that has been polluted by the touch of a Śūdra. —शूद्रोदक-पान-प्रायश्चित्त, अम्, n. a penance for drinking water given by a Śūdra.
शूद्रक: शूद्रक, अस्, m., N. of the first Āndhra king, (variously written Sindhuka, Śiśuka, and Śūraka); of a king (the author of the drama called Mṛc-chakaṭikā).
शूद्राणी: शूद्राणी, f. the wife of a Śūdra.
शून: शून शून, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्वि, q. v.), swelled, swollen, increased, grown, prospered; mor-bidly swollen; empty, vacant (Ved., Sāy. = शून्य); (अम्), n., Ved. swelling, increase, (Sāy. = सम्-ऋद्-धि, Ṛg-veda III. 33, 13); emptiness, poverty, (Sāy. = शून्य, दारिद्र्य, Ṛg-veda II. 27, 17); an in-correct pronunciation (in Vedic phonetics).
शून, अस्, आ, अम्, swollen, &c. See s. v.
शूनवत्: शून-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has increased.
शूना: शूना शूना, f. (= सूना, q. v.), the uvula or soft palate; a slaughter-house, any place where animals are killed or are liable to be destroyed, (five of these are enumerated, viz. a fire-place, a grind-stone, a broom, a mortar, and a water-pot; cf. पञ्च-सूना।) —शूना-चक्र-ध्वज-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who keeps a slaughter-house, one who has an oil-press, and one who exhibits a vintner's sign, (Manu IV. 84.) —शूना-दोष, see सूना-दोष। —शूना-वत्, आन्, m. one who keeps a slaughter-house, a butcher. —शूना-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in or brought from a slaughter-house or any place where animals are destroyed.
शून्य: शून्य शून्य, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected with शून above, fr. rt. श्वि), empty, void, hollow; vacant, barren, non-existent; utterly destitute or de-prived of, without (with inst.); ruined; nonsensical, un-meaning; guileless, unsuspicious; indifferent; lonely, private, desert, desolate, (शून्ये or शून्यम्, ind. in a lonely place, secretly); bare, naked; (अम्), n. a void, vacuum, blank; space, heaven, ether, the sky, atmosphere; a dot, spot; a cypher; naught, vacuity, nonentity, (one of the principles of Bauddha meta-physics); N. of Brahma; (आ), f. a hollow reed; a barren woman; the prickly pear; [cf. Gr. κενός, κενεός; Æol. κέννος.] —शून्य-गेह, अम्, n. an empty house. —शून्य-ता, f. or शून्य-त्व, अम्, n. emptiness, voidness, vacuity, non-existence, un-reality, the false or illusory nature of all existence. —शून्य-पदवी, f. ‘empty path,’ the road or passage of the soul, (see महा-पथ, मुद्रा-मार्ग।) —शून्य-मध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, having a hollow centre, empty inside; (अस्), m. a hollow reed. —शून्य-वत्, ind. like a cypher, annihilated or vanished as it were. —शून्य-वाद, अस्, m. the doctrine of the non-existence of anything. —शून्य-वादिन्, ई, m. ‘affirmer of non-existence,’ an atheist; a Buddhist. —शून्य-स्थान, अम्, n. an empty place. —शून्य-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, empty-handed. —शून्य-हृ-दय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘empty-hearted,’ unsuspecting, unsuspicious; absent in mind. —शून्याकृति (°य-आक्°), इस्, इस्, इ, ‘empty-formed,’ having a vacant appearance or aspect. —शून्यागार-कृतालय (°य-आग्°, °त-आल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, making an abode in de-serted houses. —शून्यालय (°य-आल्°), अस्, m. an empty or deserted house, (sleeping in such a house is forbidden.) —शून्यी-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, -कर्-तुम्, to make empty, leave.
शूपकार: शूपकार शूप-कार, अस्, m. (for सूप-कार, q. v.), one who lives by cooking for Śūdras (= शूद्र-पाकोपजीविन्).
शूयमान: शूयमान शूयमान। See under rt. श्वि।
शूर्: शूर् शूर् (also written सूर्, q. v.), cl. 4. A. शूर्यते, शुशूरे, शूरितुम्, to hurt, in-jure, kill; to be firm or motionless, stand fast, be fixed; to make firm or immovable; to be senseless; cl. 10. A. शूरयते, -यितुम्, Aor. अशुशूरत्, to be valiant or powerful, act the hero; to make great effort or exertion, (in these senses rather a Nom. fr. शूर below.)
शूर: शूर, अस्, m. (probably connected with शवस्), a hero, warrior, champion, valiant man, great or mighty man; a lion; a boar; the sun; N. of Yādava, the grandfather of Kṛṣṇa; the Śāl tree, Shorea Robusta; N. of certain other plants or trees, = चित्रक; = लकुच; = मसूर; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a tribe inhabiting Bhārata-varṣa; [cf. Zend śūra; Gr. κῦρ-ος, κυρό-ω, κύριος, κοίρανος, κοῦρος κόρος.] —शूर-कीट, अस्, m. ‘warrior-insect,’ an in-ferior hero. —शूर-ग्राम, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a multitude of heroes. —शूर-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. more heroic, very valiant. —शूर-ता, f. or शूर-त्व, अम्, n. the state or condition of a hero, heroism, prowess, valour, bravery. —शूर-देव, अस्, m., N. of the second of the twenty-four Arhats of the future Utsarpiṇī. —शूर-पुत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, having heroes as sons; (आ), f., Ved. epithet of Aditi. —शूर-पुर, अम्, n. ‘hero-town,’ N. of a town. —शूर-मठ, अस्, अम्, m. n. the college or monastery of Śūra. —शूर-मान, अम्, n. thinking one's self a hero, arrogance, vaunting. —शूर-मा-निन्, ई, m. one who thinks himself a hero, a boaster, braggart. —शूरम्-मन्य, अस्, m. one who thinks himself a hero, a boaster. —शूर-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of several kings. —शूर-वीर, अस्, m. a proper N. —शूर-श्लोक, अस्, m. a kind of arti-ficial verse; [cf. वीर-विरुद।] —शूर-साति, इस्, f., Ved. conflict of heroes, battle, war, (accord-ing to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 31, 6. शूर-साता = शूरैः सम्भजनीये युद्धे।) —शूर-सेन, अस्, m., N. of the country about Mathurā; of a king (of Mathurā and ruler of the Yadus); (आस्), m. pl., N. of the people inhabiting the above country. —शूर-सेनक, आस्, m. pl., N. of the people and country about Mathurā. —शूरसेन-ज, अस्, m. one born in Śūra-sena, an inhabitant of Śūra-sena. —शूरार्थ (°र-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, useful for or suited to heroes, for the sake of warriors. —शूरेश्वर (°र-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘lord of Śūra,’ the tutelary deity of Śūra (or the statue of a deity); a temple built by Śūra.
शूरक: शूरक, अस्, m., N. of a king (= शूद्रक).
शूरण: शूरण, अस्, आ, अम्, high-spirited (Ved., said of horses; Sāy. = विक्रम-शील, Ṛg-veda I. 163, 10); (अस्), m. a kind of esculent root, Arum Campanu-latum; the plant Bignonia Indica. —शूरणोद्भुज (°ण-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘feeding on Arum Campanu-latum,’ a kind of yellow bird (= हरिद्राङ्ग).
शूर्ण: शूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed, firm.
शूर्त: शूर्त शूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (probably) eager, quick, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 174, 6. शूर्ताः = क्षिप्राः or = क्षिप्ताः, वर्जिताः; in Naigh. II. 15. शूर्ताः is enumerated among the क्षिप्र-नामानि।)
शूर्प्: शूर्प् शूर्प् (perhaps rather a Nom. fr. शूर्प below), cl. 10. P. शूर्पयति, -यि-तुम्, to measure, mete out.
शूर्प: शूर्प, अस्, अम्, m. n. (according to Uṇādi-s. III. 26. fr. rt. शॄ; also written सूर्प), a winnowing basket or a kind of wicker receptacle which, when shaken about, serves as a fan for winnowing corn; (अस्), m. a measure of two Droṇas; (ई), f. a small winnowing basket or fan; a toy for children; N. of the sister of Rāvaṇa, (see शूर्प-णखा।) —शूर्प-कर्ण, अस्, m. ‘having ears like winnowing fans,’ an elephant. —शूर्प-णखा, f. or शूर्प-णखी, f. ‘having finger-nails like winnowing fans,’ N. of the sister of the Daitya Rāvaṇa, (she fell in love with Rāma and, being rejected by him, attacked Sītā, but was beaten off and mutilated by Lakṣmaṇa; in revenge she incited her brother to carry off Sītā.) —शूर्प-निष्पाव, अस्, m. a basket-full of win-nowed corn. —शूर्प-पर्णी, f. a sort of bean, Phaseolus Trilobus. —शूर्प-वात, अस्, m. the wind raised by shaking a winnowing basket. —शूर्प-श्रुति, इस्, m. ‘having ears like winnowing fans,’ an elephant.
शूर्पक: शूर्पक, अस्, m., N. of a demon (an enemy of Kāma-deva). —शूर्पकाराति or शूर्पकारि (°क-अर्°), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Śūrpaka,’ epithet of Kāma (god of love).
शूर्पी: शूर्पी, f. See above under शूर्प।
शूर्पारक: शूर्पारक शूर्पारक, N. of a mythical country.
शूर्म: शूर्म शूर्म, अस्, m. an iron image; an anvil.
शूर्मि: शूर्मि, इस्, m. f. or शूर्मिका or शूर्मी, f. = शूर्म above; [cf. सूर्मि, स्युर्मि।]
शूल्: शूल् शूल् (rather a Nom. fr. शूल below), cl. 1. P. शूलति, शुशूल, शूलितुम्, to be ill; to disorder, make sick, disease; to pierce, transfix, impale; to cry, make a loud noise; to collect (?).
शूल: शूल, अस्, अम्, m. n. any sharp or acute pain; pain in the stomach, colic; rheumatism, gout; any sharp or pointed weapon, a pike, dart, spear, lance, spike; the trident of Śiva; a sharp iron pin or spit (on which meat is roasted); a stake for impaling criminals; a banner, ensign; the ninth astronomical Yoga; death, dying; (आ), f. a stake for impaling criminals; a harlot, prostitute; [cf. Slav. sūliza.] —शूल-गव, a kind of animal sacrifice. —शूल-ग्रन्थि, इस्, f. ‘having sharp knots,’ a kind of Dūrvā grass (= माला-दूर्वा). —शूल-घातन, अम्, n. ‘pain-destroying,’ iron rust or filings. —शूल-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, removing or allaying sharp pain, sedative, anodyne; (अस्), m. a kind of plant (= तुम्बुरु)। —शूल-द्विष्, ट्, m. ‘enemy to colic,’ Asa Fetida. —शूल-धन्वन्, आ, m. ‘having a trident for a bow,’ epithet of Śiva. —शूल-धर, अस्, m. ‘spear-holder, trident-holder,’ epithet of Śiva; (आ), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-धारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, spear-holding, lance-bearing, trident-holding; (इणी), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-धृक्, m. (see धृक्, p. 459), ‘trident-bearing,’ epithet of Śiva; (क्), f. epithet of Durgā. —शूल-नाशन, अम्, n. ‘remov-ing pain in the stomach,’ white sochal salt. —शूल-पत्त्री, f. a kind of grass (= शूली). —शूल-पाणि, इस्, m. ‘trident-handed,’ epithet of Śiva (regarded as the king of the Bhūtas); N. of the author of the Prāyaścitta-viveka and of the Tithi-dvaidha-prakaraṇa and of the Yājñavalkya-ṭīkā. —शूल-पाणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, holding or bearing a lance or spear. —शूल-भृत्, त्, m. ‘spear-holder,’ an epithet of Śiva. —शूल-भेद, अस्, m., N. of a place. —शूल-मुद्गर-हस्त, अस्, आ, अम्, having a lance and mace in hand, armed with a lance and club. —शूल-वेदना, f. sharp or acute pain. —शूल-शत्रु, उस्, m. ‘hostile to colic,’ the castor-oil plant, Ricinus Communis. —शूल-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, fixed on a stake, impaled. —शूल-हन्त्री, f. ‘colic-removing,’ a kind of barley (= यवानी). —शूल-हस्त, अस्, m. ‘lance-handed,’ a man armed with a lance, lancer, pikeman. —शूल-हृत्, त्, m. ‘removing colic,’ Asa Fetida. —शूला-कृ, cl. 8. P. -करोति, &c., to roast on a spit. —शूलाकृत (°ल-आक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, roasted on a spit, &c.; (अम्), n. roasted meat. —शूलाग्र (°ल-अग्°), अम्, n. the point of a pike or stake, &c. —शूलेश्वरी-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —शू-लोत्खा (°ल-उत्°), f. the medicinal plant Serratula Anthelmintica. —शूलोद्यत-कर (°ल-उद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, with uplifted spear in hand.
शूलक: शूलक, अस्, m. a restive or unbroken horse; [cf. शूकल।]
शूलिक: शूलिक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a spear or any sharp instrument; roasted on a spit; (अस्), m. a hare; (अम्), n. roast meat.
शूलिन्: शूलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, suffering sharp pain, suffering from colic; armed with a spear or pike, carrying a lance or stake; (ई), m. a spearman, pikeman, lancer; epithet of Śiva (as holding a trident); a hare; N. of a Muni; (इनी), f. epithet of Durgā.
शूलिन: शूलिन, अस्, m. the Indian fig-tree (= भाण्डीर).
शूली: शूली, f. a kind of grass (= मधु-लता).
शूल्य: शूल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, roasted on a spit; deserving impalement; (अम्), n. roasted meat. —शूल्य-पाक, अस्, m. any meat or other substance roasted on a spit. —शूल्य-मांस, अम्, n. roast meat, meat cooked on a spit.
शूशुजान: शूशुजान शूशुजान, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Sāy. = शोशुचान, दीप्यमान, Ṛg-veda X. 34, 6; cf. शुशुचान, p. 1013), Ved. glowing, resplen-dent.
शूशुवस्: शूशुवस् शूशुवस्, वान्, m. (fr. rt. श्वि), Ved. one who has increased, increasing; large.
शूशुवान: शूशुवान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. growing in size, in-creasing in strength.
शूष्: शूष् शूष् (also written सूष्), cl. 1. P. शूषति, शुशूष, शूषितुम्, to bring forth; to beget, propagate.
शूष: शूष शूष, अम्, n. (perhaps connected with rt. श्वि), Ved. strength, (according to Naigh. II. 9, Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 154, 3 = बल; cf. शुष्म; in Naigh. III. 6 = सुख); (अस्), m., N. of a pre-ceptor.
शूषणि: शूषणि, in Ṛg-veda X. 93, 1. probably fr. a base शूषन्; regarded by some as a kind of Ved. Inf. fr. rt. श्वि।
शृकाल: शृकाल शृकाल, अस्, m. (for शृगाल below), a jackal.
शृगाल: शृगाल शृगाल, अस्, m. (etymology doubt-ful, but cf. Gr. κραγέτης; perhaps connected with rt. शॄ; sometimes written सृगाल), a jackal; a rogue, cheat; a coward, poltroon; an ill-natured or harsh-speaking man; N. of a demon; epithet of Kṛṣṇa; (ई), f. a female jackal; a fox; flight, re-treat; a kind of plant (= कोकिलाक्ष); another plant (= विदारी). —शृगाल-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘jackal's thorn,’ a kind of plant, Zizyphus Scandens. —शृगाल-कोलि, इस्, m. a sort of jujube. —शृगाल-घण्टी, f. a particular plant (= कोकिलाक्ष). —शृ-गाल-जम्बु, उस्, or शृगाल-जम्बू, ऊस्, f. a kind of cucumber, Cucumis Madraspatanus; the fruit of the jujube. —शृगाल-जाति, इस्, f. birth (in a future life) as a jackal. —शृगाल-योनि, इस्, m. f. the womb of a jackal; the being born in a future birth as a jackal. —शृगाल-रूप, अस्, m. ‘jackal-formed,’ epi-thet of Śiva. —शृगाल-विन्ना, f. a kind of plant (= पृश्नि-पर्णी).
शृगालिका: शृगालिका, f. a female jackal; a fox; running away, flight, retreat; a kind of plant (= भूमि-कुष्माण्ड); a proper N.
शृङ्खल: शृङ्खल शृङ्खल, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. (ety-mology doubtful; perhaps connected with शिञ्जा, ‘a tinkling sound’), an iron chain; any chain or fetter; a belt or chain worn round the waist for ornament, &c.; an iron chain for confining the feet of an elephant; a measuring chain. —शृङ्खल-ता, f. or शृङ्खल-त्व, अम्, n. the being chained together; restraint; concatenation, connection, order; a series. —शृङ्खला-बन्ध or शृङ्खला-बन्धन, अम्, n. confining by chains or fetters.
शृङ्खलक: शृङ्खलक, अस्, m. a chain; a young camel or other young animal with wooden rings or clogs on his feet (to prevent his straying); any camel.
शृङ्खलित: शृङ्खलित, अस्, आ, अम्, chained, fettered, bound, confined.
शृङ्खली: शृङ्खली, f. a kind of plant (= कोकिलाक्ष).
शृङ्ग: शृङ्ग शृङ्ग, अम्, n. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 125. fr. rt. शॄ with affix ग, a nasal being inserted; according to some perhaps contracted fr. शिरङ्-ग, ‘head-going’), a horn; the top or summit of a mountain, a peak, crag; the summit of a building, pinnacle, turret; any peak or point or projection or lofty object; a cusp or horn of the moon; height, elevation, dignity, lordship, mastership, supremacy, sovereignty; the rising or bursting forth of desire, excess of love or passion; anything sharp or fine-pointed; a fountain or artificial spout of water; any horn-like vessel or instrument; a buffalo's horn or other horn used for blowing; a lotus; a mark, token, sign; (अस्), m. a medicinal plant and root (= जी-वक); N. of a Ṛṣi or Muni (of whom, in some parts of India, on occasions of drought, earthen images are said to be made and supplicated for rain); [cf. Gr. κέρας; Lat. cornu; Goth. haurn; Angl. Sax. horn.] —शृङ्ग-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= शृङ्गाटक). —शृङ्ग-गिरि, इस्, m., N. of a mountain. —शृङ्ग-ग्राहिका, f. (in logic) dis-tribution, taking singly and severally all the parti-culars included under a general term or all the indi-viduals composing a body. —शृङ्ग-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, horn-produced, made from horn; produced on mountain-peaks; (अस्), m. an arrow, shaft; (अम्), n. the aloe wood or tree (= अ-गुरु). —शृङ्ग-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —शृङ्ग-प्रहारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, horn-striking, butting or fighting with the horns. —शृङ्ग-प्रिय, अस्, m. epithet of Śiva. —शृङ्ग-मूल, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= शृङ्गाटक)। —शृङ्ग-मोहिन्, ई, m. the Campaka tree. —शृङ्ग-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having peaks, peaked; (आन्), m. a mountain; epithet of a mythical moun-tain forming one of the boundaries of the earth. —शृङ्ग-वृष्, ट्, m., Ved. epithet of the Sun; N. of a Ṛṣi (said to have been the father of Indra; शृङ्ग-वृषो नपात्, the offspring of Śṛṅga-vṛṣ, i. e. Indra). —शृङ्ग-वेर, अम्, n. ginger (undried or dry); N. of a town (= गुह-चण्डाल-पुर)। —शृङ्ग-वेरक, अम्, n. ginger. —शृङ्गवेरा-भ-मूलक (°र-आभ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘having a root like that of ginger,’ a kind of grass (= एरका)। —शृङ्ग-शत, अम्, n. a hundred peaks. —शृङ्-गाग्र-प्रहरणाभिमुख (°ग-अग्°, °ण-अभ्°), अस्, ई, अम्, advancing towards or making a charge with the weapons of the points of the horns; ready to strike with the points of the horns. —शृङ्गान्-तर (°ग-अन्°), अम्, n. the space or interval be-tween the horns (of a cow &c.). —शृङ्गीश्वर-तीर्थ (°गी-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —शृङ्गोच्-छ्राय (°ग-उच्°), अस्, m. a lofty peak. —शृङ्गोन्-नति (°ग-उन्°), इस्, f. elevation of a horn, the rising (of the moon?; cf. शीर्षोदय).
शृङ्गक: शृङ्गक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a horn; anything pointed; a cusp or horn of the moon; (अस्), m. a medicinal root, (commonly called Jīvaka.)
शृङ्गला: शृङ्गला, f. a particular plant (= अज-शृङ्गी, ‘goat's horn’).
शृङ्गाट: शृङ्गाट, अम्, n. a place where four roads meet; (अस्), m. the aquatic plant Trapa Bispinosa; the shrub Ruellia or Barleria Longifolia.
शृङ्गाटक: शृङ्गाटक, अम्, n. a place where four roads meet; a kind of pastry or dish of minced meat, &c. (called Samūsā in Hindī); a door; (अस्), m. the aquatic plant Trapa Bispinosa; a mountain having three peaks.
शृङ्गार: शृङ्गार, अस्, m. (probably connected with शृङ्ग in the sense of ‘rising of desire;’ according to Uṇādi-s. III. 136. fr. rt. शॄ with affix आर, a nasal and ग् being inserted), love, sexual passion, erotic sen-timent; sexual union, coition; a dress suitable for amorous purposes, an elegant dress; a mark or marks with red-lead on an elephant's head and trunk by way of ornament; any mark; N. of the father of Jaya-ratha; (अम्), n. cloves; red-lead; fragrant powder for the dress or person; undried ginger; Agallochum. —शृङ्गार-चेष्टा, f. love-gesture, any outward action indicating love. —शृङ्गार-तिलक, अम्, n., N. of an erotic poem by Rudra-bhaṭṭa. —शृङ्गार-भाषित, अम्, n. a love story. —शृङ्-गार-भूषण, अम्, n. red-lead. —शृङ्गार-मण्डप, N. of a temple. —शृङ्गार-योनि, इस्, m. ‘love-source,’ epithet of Kāma, god of love. —शृङ्गार-रस, अस्, m. the erotic sentiment. —शृङ्गाररसाष्टक (°स-अष्°), अम्, n., N. of eight stanzas by Kālidāsa on the erotic sentiment. —शृङ्गार-वती, f., N. of a town; of a queen. —शृङ्गार-विधि, इस्, m. a dress suitable for amorous interviews. —शृङ्गार-वेश, अस्, आ, अम्, dressed suitably for amorous enterprises. —शृङ्गार-शत or शृङ्गार-शतक, अम्, n. ‘a hundred verses on love,’ N. of the second book of Bhartṛ-hari's poem. —शृङ्गार-सहाय, अस्, m. an assistant in affairs of love, confidant of a dramatic hero. —शृङ्-गारैक-रस (°र-एक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, whose sole feeling is love.
शृङ्गारक: शृङ्गारक, अस्, आ, अम्, horned, having a horn or crest; (अस्), m. love, &c. = शृङ्गार; (अम्), n. red-lead.
शृङ्गारित: शृङ्गारित, अस्, आ, अम्, affected by love, impas-sioned; stained with red-lead, reddened; adorned, decorated, embellished.
शृङ्गारिन्: शृङ्गारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, feeling love or amorous pas-sion; full of love, amorous, enamoured, impassioned; relating to love; stained with red-lead; (ई), m. an impassioned lover; an elephant; dress, decoration; the Areca or betel-nut tree; a ruby (= माणिक्य).
शृङ्गि: शृङ्गि, इस्, f. a species of Silurus or sheat-fish; (इस्), m. gold for ornaments, (said to be also शृङ्गि, n.; cf. शृङ्गी।) —शृङ्गि-कनक, अम्, n. gold used for ornaments.
शृङ्गिक: शृङ्गिक, अम्, n. a sort of poison; (आ), f. a kind of Betula or birch tree (= प्रति-विषा).
शृङ्गिण: शृङ्गिण, अस्, आ, अम्, horned; (अस्), m. a ram.
शृङ्गिन्: शृङ्गिन्, ई, इणी, इ, horned; crested, peaked; (ई), m. a mountain; N. of a mythical mountain forming one of the boundaries of the earth, (Viṣṇu-Purāṇa II. 2); an elephant; a tree; N. of a son of Gautama; epithet of Śiva; (इणी), f. a cow; Arabian jasmine or another species; heart-pea; the plant Kaṭukī.
शृङ्गी: शृङ्गी, f. a kind of gold used for making orna-ments; a sort of Silurus or sheat-fish; a particular medicinal root shaped like a bull's horn (= ऋष-भ); a kind of poison; a kind of Betula; N. of various other plants and trees (= अति-विषा; = कर्-कट-शृङ्गी; = प्लक्ष; = वट). —शृङ्गी-क-नक, अम्, n. a kind of gold used for ornaments.
शृङ्गेरिपुर: शृङ्गेरि-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town.
शृणि: शृणि शृणि, इस्, f. (said to be fr. rt. शॄ), the hook for goading an elephant, (also written सृणि।)
शृण्वत्: शृण्वत् शृण्वत्। See under rt. 1. श्रु।
शृण्वत्, अन्, अती, अत्, hearing, listening to, hearken-ing.
शृत: शृत शृत, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. श्रा), boiled, (used especially with reference to water, milk, and ghee); cooked, dressed; [cf. श्राण, श्रपित।] —शृत-पा, आस्, आस्, अम् (see 2. and 4. पा), Ved. a drinker or appropriator of an oblation, (Sāy. = क्षी-रादेर् हविषः पातृ, Ṛg-veda VII. 18, 16.) —शृत-पाक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. having a well-performed cooking, cooked or dressed fit for the gods, (Sāy. = देव-योग्य-पाकोपेत, Ṛg-veda I. 162, 10.)
शृत, अस्, आ, अम्, boiled, &c. See s. v.
शृध्: शृध् शृध्, cl. 1. A. (also P. in Fut., Aor., Cond.) शर्धते, शशृधे, शर्-धिष्यते (and शर्त्स्यति), अशृधत्, &c., शर्धि-तुम्, to break wind downwards; cl. 1. P. A. शर्-धति, -ते, to moisten, become moist or wet; cl. 10. P. शर्धयति, to insult (by breaking wind against or by voiding excrement), mock at, ridicule; to strive, make effort, (in this sense also cl. 1. P. according to some): Caus. शर्धयति, -यितुम्: Desid. शिशर्धिषते, शिशृत्सति: Intens. शरीशृ-ध्यते, शरीशर्द्धि।
शृद्ध: शृद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, expelled from the body (as wind); moistened.
शृद्ध्वा: शृद्ध्वा, ind. having expelled wind from the body.
शृधु: शृधु, उस्, m. f. (according to Śabda-k. only m.), the anus; = बुद्धि।
शृधू: शृधू, ऊस्, m. f. (according to Śabda-k. only m.), the anus; = कुत्सित।
शृध्या: शृध्या, f., Ved. effort, success, (Sāy. = उत्साह-नीयं कर्म, Ṛg-veda II. 12, 10.)
शॄ: शॄ शॄ, cl. 9. P. शृणाति, शशार (3rd pl. शशरुः and शश्रुः, Pāṇ. VII. 4, 12), शरिष्यति or शरीष्यति, अशारीत्, शरितुम्, शरी-तुम् (Ved. Inf. शरीतोस्), to injure, hurt, wound, kill, destroy; to tear or split in pieces, break, tear asunder: Pass. शीर्यते (ep. also -ति), to be injured; to be broken or torn or shattered, be split to pieces; to wither, moulder, decay, waste away: Caus. शार-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशीशरत्: Desid. शिशरिषति or शिशरीषति or शिशीर्षति: Intens. शेशीर्यते, शाशर्ति; [cf. Zend śūra: Gr. κείρω, κορ-μός, κέρμα, κουρά, κουρεύ-ς, κεραΐζω, κέρασ, κεραός, κλάω, κλῆρος, κολαβός, (probably) κορύνη: Lat. cur-tu-s (Sabin. curi-s); cornu, cervus; clava, quiris, (probably) in-columis: Goth. hair-u-s, ‘a sword;’ haurn: Old Norse hior: Old Sax. her-u: Angl. Sax. hyrt; horn; heorot, heort: Slav. kor-a.]
शृणान: शृणान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. hurting, injuring.
शेखर: शेखर शेखर, अस्, m. (fr. शिखर; the more usual form would be शैखर), a crest, chap-let, diadem, crown, tuft, garland of flowers worn on the top of the head; a peak, summit; the chief or head of anything (generally at the end of comps.); a particular Dhruva or recurring stanza of a song, (another kind is called लघु-शेखर); a proper N.; (अम्), n. cloves; the root of the Hyperanthera Moringa.
शेखरित: शेखरित, अस्, आ, अम्, crested, tufted, topped, peaked.
शेखरी: शेखरी, f. a particular parasitical plant (= वन्दा).
शेणवी: शेणवी शेणवी or शेणा, f. (doubtful), under-standing, mind, intellect.
शेप: शेप शेप, अस्, m. or शेपस्, अस्, n. (perhaps connected with rt. 3. शप्, see Nirukta III. 21; ac-cording to Uṇādi-s. IV. 200. fr. rt. 1. शी), the penis or male organ; a testicle; a tail. —शेप-हर्षण, अस्, ई, अम्, exciting the male organ, see Atharva-veda Prātiśākhya II. 56.
शेफ: शेफ, अस्, m. (also written सेफ), or शेफस्, अस्, n. the male organ, penis; a testicle; a tail.
शेपान: शेपान शेपान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 3. शप्), Ved. one who has sworn, bound by oath.
शेपाल: शेपाल शेपाल, अस्, m. the aquatic plant Vallisneria (= शेवाल).
शेफालि: शेफालि शेफालि, इस्, f. a kind of plant, Nyctanthes Arbor Tristis; another plant (= निर्-गुण्टी).
शेफालिका: शेफालिका or शेफाली, f. = शेफालि above.
शेमुषी: शेमुषी शेमुषी, f. (probably fem. of the perf. part. of rt. 1. शम्), understanding, intellect.
शेल्: शेल् शेल् (also written सेल्), cl. 1. P. शे-लति, Caus. Aor. अशिशेलत्, to go, move about; to shake, tremble.
शेलु: शेलु शेलु, उस्, m. a kind of plant or small tree, Cordia Myxa; a kind of fruit.
शेव्: शेव् शेव् (another form of rt. सेव्), cl. 1. A. शेवते, &c., to worship, serve.
शेव: शेव शेव, अस्, आ, अम् (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 152, 154. fr. rt. 1. शी, but more probably con-nected with rt. श्वि and शवस्, cf. शिव), causing happiness, propitious, affectionate (Ved., Sāy. = सु-ख-कर); (अस्), m. a snake; height, elevation; happiness; treasure, wealth; an epithet of Agni (as being the source of happiness, Sāy. = सुख-कर); of Soma; the male organ, = शेप; (अम्), n. happi-ness; (अम्), ind. hail, homage, an exclamation or salutation addressed to the deities; (अम्, आ), n. f. the male organ, penis (= शेप). —शेव-धि, इस्, m. (also written सेव-धि), ‘wealth-receptacle,’ one of the nine treasures of Kuvera, divine treasure, any valuable treasure; [cf. नि-धि।] —शेवधि-पा, आस्, m., Ved. a lord of treasures.
शेवृध्: शे-वृध्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. conferring happiness, (Sāy. शे-वृधः = शेवस्य, सुखस्य वर्धयितारः, Ṛg-veda V. 87, 4.)
शेवृध: शे-वृध, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. increasing or con-tributing to felicity, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda III. 16, 2. appears to derive शे-वृध fr. 2. शम् and rt. वृध्); (अम्), n. happiness (enumerated among the सुख-नामानि in Naigh. III. 6).
शेव्य: शेव्य, अस्, m., Ved. a giver of happiness, (Sāy. = साधुः सुख-कर्ता, Ṛg-veda I. 156, 1.)
शेवल: शेवल शेवल, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. 1. शी, cf. शैवल), the aquatic plant Vallisneria Octandra [cf. शेपाल]; the green moss-like sub-stance growing on the surface of stagnant water, duck-weed, (said to be also अस्, m.)
शेवलिनी: शेवलिनी, f. ‘having Śevala,’ a river; [cf. शैवलिन्।]
शेवाली: शेवाली, f. a kind of plant (= आकाश-मांसी).
शेश्यित: शेश्यित शेश्यित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. शी, Pāṇ. I. 2, 19), fast asleep, sleeping much. —शेश्यित-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, one who has slept soundly, sleeping much or soundly.
शेश्वीयमान: शेश्वीयमान शेश्वीयमान। See under rt. श्वि।
शेश्वीयमान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. swelling or in-creasing excessively, enlarging, expanding.
शेष: शेष शेष, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 2. शिष्), re-maining, other, all the other; (अस्, अम्), m. n. remainder, leavings, rest, residue, surplus, balance; the being spared or left, escape, salvation, reprieve, respite; anything rejected, anything left or left out or omitted or left to be supplied; anything left out or omitted to be said, (इति शेषः, ‘so it was intended to be said,’ a phrase used by commentators in sup-plying any word or words necessary to elucidate the text); (अस्), m. result, issue, effect, conclusion, end, termination; finish, destruction, death, killing; N. of a celebrated mythological thousand-headed serpent regarded as the emblem of eternity (whence he is also called An-anta, ‘the infinite;’ in the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa he and the serpents Vāsuki and Takṣaka are described as sons of Kadru, but in one place Śeṣa alone is called king of the Nāgas or snakes inhabiting Pātāla, while elsewhere Vāsuki also is described as king of the Nāgas and Takṣaka of the serpents; the thousand-headed Śeṣa is sometimes represented as forming the couch and canopy of Viṣṇu whilst sleeping during the intervals of creation, sometimes as bearing the entire world on one of his heads, sometimes as supporting the seven Pātālas; he is said to have taught astronomy to Garga; ac-cording to some legends he became incarnate in Bala-rāma, see बल-राम); N. of Bala-rāma, (see above); N. of one of the Prajā-patis; of a Muni; (अम्), n. the remnants of food; the temples dedicated to him in his popular symbol of the Liṅga [see शिव] are very numerous every-where, but the doctrines of the Śaivas as represented by their great teachers, such as Śaṅkara, are too philosophical for the majority of the people, who are more attracted by Viṣṇu, especially in his forms of Kṛṣṇa and Rāma: various divisions of Śaiva sects have prevailed at different times, the earlier divisions being those of the Raudras who have the Tri-śūla or trident marked on their foreheads, the Ugras who have the Ḍamaru or drum on their arms, the Bhāktas who have the Liṅga on their foreheads, the Jaṅgamas who have that symbol on their heads, and the Pāśupatas who have it marked on other parts of their bodies; शोण्: शोण् शोण् (perhaps to be regarded as a Nom. fr. शोण below), cl. 1. P. शोणति, शुशोण, शोणितुम्, to be or become red; to go, move, approach: Caus. शोणयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशुशोणत्।
शोण: शोण, अस्, आ or ई, अम् (thought by some to be fr. स-वर्ण), coloured like the red lotus, red, crimson, of a crimson or chesnut colour; red in the face (from passion &c.); brown, bay; yellow; (अस्), m. the colour of the red lotus, red, crimson (the colour); fire or the god of fire; a sort of red sugar-cane; a chesnut or bay horse; a particular ocean; the river Śoṇa or Sone (sometimes written शोणा, f.; it rises in Gondwana in the district of Nagpore, on the table-land of Amara-kaṇṭaka, four or five miles east of the source of the Narma-dā or Nerbudda, and running first northerly and then easterly for five hundred miles falls into the Ganges above Pāṭali-putra or Patna); the plant Bignonia Indica; a proper N.; (अम्), n. blood; red-lead, minium; [cf. Slav. sini.] —शोण-झिण्टिका, f. a kind of red Barleria. —शोण-झिण्टी, f., N. of two plants (= कुरुवक, कण्टकिनी). —शोण-नद, N. of a river. —शोण-पत्त्र, अस्, m. ‘red-leaved,’ a red kind of hogweed. —शोण-पद्मक, अम्, n. a red lotus. —शोण-पुष्पक, अस्, m. ‘red-flowered,’ the Kovidāra tree. —शोण-पुष्पी, f. ‘red-flowered,’ a kind of plant (= सिन्दूर-पुष्पी). —शोण-रत्न, अम्, n. a red gem; a ruby. —शोण-सङ्गम, अस्, m. ‘Śoṇa-con-fluence,’ N. of a place. —शोणाम्बु (°ण-अम्°), उस्, m. ‘having crimson waters or having waters of blood,’ N. of one of the seven clouds at the destruc-tion of the world. —शोणाश्मन् (°ण-अश्°), आ, m. a red stone; a ruby. —शोणोपल (°ण-उप्°), अस्, m. a red stone; a ruby. —शोणोल्लीढ (°ण-उल्°), अस्, आ, अम्, sharpened or polished on a whetstone.
शोणक: शोणक, अस्, m. the plant Bignonia or Calosanthes Indica, (this plant has many synonyms; cf. कुटन्-नट, नट, मण्डूक-पर्ण।)
शोणित: शोणित, अस्, आ, अम्, red, crimson, purple; (अम्), n. blood; saffron. —शोणित-चन्दन, अम्, n. red sandal. —शोणित-प, अस्, आ, अम्, drinking blood; blood-sucking. —शोणित-पारणा, f. ‘breakfast of blood,’ a meal of flesh-meat. —शोणित-पुर, अम्, n. the city of the Asura Vāṇa (= वाण-पुर)। —शोणित-वर्णन, अम्, n. description of the nature and properties of blood. —शोणित-वर्णनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, treating of the above. —शोणित-विन्दु-वर्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, showering drops of blood. —शोणित-स्नात, अस्, आ, अम्, bathed in blood. —शोणितादिग्ध (°त-आद्°), अस्, आ, अम्, blood-stained. —शोणितार्शिन् (°त-अर्°), ई, इनी, इ, suffering from piles attended with excretions of blood. —शोणिताह्वय (°त-आह्°), अम्, n. ‘blood-named,’ saffron. —शोणितोक्षित (°त-उक्°), अस्, आ, अम्, blood-stained, sprinkled with blood. —शोणितोत्पल (°त-उत्°), अम्, n. a red lotus. —शो-णितोपल (°त-उप्°), अस्, m. ‘blood-stone,’ a ruby, (according to some also अम्, n.) —शोणितौघ (°त-ओघ), अस्, m. a torrent or stream of blood.
शोणिमन्: शोणिमन्, आ, m. redness, the quality of being red.
शोथ: शोथ शोथ, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. II. 4. fr. rt. शु, ‘to go;’ evidently connected with rt. श्वि), swelling, intumescence, tumefaction from disease, dropsy. —शोथ-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying or removing swellings, discutient; (ई), f. hogweed, Boerhavia Diffusa; a kind of shrub (= शाल-पर्णी)। —शोथ-जित्, त्, त्, त्, overcoming or removing swell-ings, discutient; (त्), f. hogweed; the marking-nut plant. —शोथ-जिह्म, अस्, m. hogweed. —शोथ-रोग, अस्, m. ‘swelling disease,’ dropsy. —शोथ-रोगिन्, ई, इणी, इ, suffering from dropsy, dropsical. —शोथ-हृत्, त्, त्, त्, removing swellings, discutient; (त्), m. the marking-nut plant.
शोपारीपाक: शोपारीपाक शोपारी-पाक, a particular me-dicinal decoction.
शोफ: शोफ शोफ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. श्वि; cf. शोथ), intumescence, morbid swelling, tumefaction, bloated-ness, flabbiness. —शोफ-घ्नी, f. a kind of shrub (= शाल-पर्णी); a kind of red hogweed. —शोफ-नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, removing swellings; (अस्), m. a kind of tree (= नील). —शोफ-हृत्, त्, त्, त्, re-moving swellings; (त्), m. the marking-nut plant.
शोशुचत्: शोशुचत् शोशुचत्, अत्, अती, अत् (fr. Intens. of rt. 3. शुच्), Ved. shining very brightly, very splendid.
शोशुचान: शोशुचान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. shining very brightly, very radiant, resplendent; [cf. शुशुचान।]
शोशुच्यमान: शोशुच्यमान शोशुच्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. शुच्), sorrowing intensely, grieving deeply.
शोशुभ्यमान: शोशुभ्यमान शोशुभ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Intens. of rt. 1. शुभ्), shining very much, very brilliant.
शोस्: शोस् शोस् (?), ind. a particle of reproach or contempt.
शौक: शौक शौक, अम्, n. (fr. शुक), a flock of parrots; (fr. शोक?), sorrowfulness, (according to Śabda-k. = स्त्रीणां करणम्, for करुणम्?).
शौकर: शौकर शौकर or शौकरव, अम्, n., N. of a particular Tīrtha (described in a chapter of the Vārāha-Purāṇa called Jambūkopākhyāna).
शौक्त: शौक्त शौक्त, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्त), acid, acetic, acetous.
शौक्तिक: 1. शौक्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, acid, acetic.
शौक्तिक 2. शौक्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्ति), relating to a pearl.
शौक्तेय: शौक्तेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to a pearl; (अम्), n. a pearl.
शौक्र: शौक्र शौक्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुक्र), seminal, relating to sperm, &c.
शौक्लिकेय: शौक्लिकेय शौक्लिकेय, अस्, m. a sort of poison, (probably for शौल्किकेय, q. v.)
शौक्ल्य: शौक्ल्य शौक्ल्य, अम्, n. (fr. शुक्ल), white-ness, clearness.
शौङ्ग: शौङ्ग शौङ्ग, आस्, m. pl., N. of a Gotra.
शौङ्गीपुत्र: शौङ्गी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a teacher.
शौङ्गेय: शौङ्गेय शौङ्गेय, अस्, m. (doubtful), epi-thet of Garuḍa or a black-winged enemy of birds.
शौच: शौच शौच, अम्, n. (fr. शुचि), purification from personal defilement (especially from defilement caused by the death of a relation &c.); evacuation of excrement; freedom from defilement, purity, cleanness; honesty; (अस्), m. a proper N. —शौच-कल्प, अस्, m. mode of purification, purificatory rite. —शौच-कूप, अस्, m. ‘cleansing-pit,’ a privy. —शौच-त्व, अम्, n. purity. —शौच-विधि, इस्, m. rule of purifi-cation (after defilement by the death of a relation &c.), directions for cleansing the person. —शौचा-चार (°च-आच्°), अस्, m. a purificatory rite, rule of purification established by immemorial custom, mode of cleansing the person by ablution &c. (after voiding excrement or contracting any defilement). —शौचेप्सु (°च-ईप्°), उस्, उस्, उ, wishing or intending to obtain purification.
शौचिक: शौचिक, अस्, m. a cleanser, cleaner; a particular mixed caste (the son of a Śauṇḍika and a Kaivarta woman).
शौचिवृक्षि: शौचिवृक्षि, इस्, m., N. of an author.
शौचेय: शौचेय, अस्, m. a washerman; a proper N.
शौचद्रथ: शौचद्रथ शौचद्रथ, अस्, m., Ved. a patro-nymic of a descendant of Śucad-ratha.
शौट्: शौट् शौट् (also written शौड्), cl. 1. P. शौटति, शुशौट, शौटितुम्, to be proud or haughty: Caus. शौटयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशु-शौटत्।
शौटीर: शौटीर, अस्, आ, अम्, proud, haughty; (अस्), m. a hero; a proud or haughty man (but of low tribe or occupation); an upstart; one who abandons the world, an ascetic.
शौटीर्य: शौटीर्य, अम्, n. pride, arrogance; heroism, prowess.
शौड्: शौड् शौड् (= rt. शौट्), cl. 1. P. शौडति, &c., to be proud or haughty.
शौड: शौड, अस्, m., N. of a country.
शौण्डर्य: शौण्डर्य, अम्, n. pride, arrogance; [cf. शौ-टीर्य।]
शौण्डीर: शौण्डीर, अस्, आ, अम्, proud, haughty; elevated, looking upwards; (also written शौण्डिर, शौडीर।) —शौण्डीर-ता, f. haughtiness, pride.
शौण्ड: शौण्ड शौण्ड, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुण्डा), fond of spirituous liquor, addicted to drinking; drunk, in-toxicated; (ई), f. long pepper; another sort (= चव्य).
शौण्डिक: शौण्डिक, अस्, m. a distiller and vender of spirituous liquors, vintner; a particular mixed caste (the son of a Kaivarta and a Gāndhika woman); (ई), f. a female vintner or keeper of a tavern or dram shop (regarded as one of the eight Akulas according to the Śāktas).
शौण्डीक: शौण्डीक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a tribe.
शौद्धाक्षर: शौद्धाक्षर शौद्धाक्षर, अस्, m., scil. सन्-धि, epithet of a particular Sandhi, (viz. the insertion of श् before चन्द्र, e. g. पुरु-श्-चन्द्र; of ष् be-fore कृ, e. g. परि-ष्-कृण्वन्, &c.)
शौद्धोदनि: शौद्धोदनि शौद्धोदनि, इस्, m. (fr. शुद्धो-दन), ‘son of Śuddhodana,’ a patronymic of the great Buddha (founder of the Buddhist religion, see बुद्ध).
शौद्र: शौद्र शौद्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूद्र), servile, relating or belonging to the Śūdra or lowest tribe; (अस्), m. the son of a man of either of the first three classes by a Śūdra woman, (the last of the twelve kinds of sons acknowledged in the ancient Hindū law.)
शौधिका: शौधिका शौधिका, f. a variety of panic, (Panicum Italicum, = रक्त-कङ्गु।)
शौन: शौन शौन, अम्, n. (fr. शूना), meat kept at a slaughter-house.
शौनिक: शौनिक, अस्, m. a butcher, poulterer, vender of the flesh of beasts or birds; chase, hunting.
शौनक: शौनक शौनक, अस्, m., N. of the reputed author of the Ṛg-veda Prātiśākhya and of certain Kalpa-sūtras and various other Vedic compositions and works on law, (he is described as the teacher of Kātyāyana and especially of Āśvalāyana; he is said to have united the Bāṣkala and Śākala Śākhās, and is sometimes identified with the Vedic Ṛṣi Gṛtsa-mada; but according to the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa, Śaunaka was a son of Gṛtsa-mada, and originated the system of four castes; the various legends about him are very confused.) —शौनक-कल्प-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of certain Kalpa-sūtras (ascribed to Śaunaka and supposed to have been destroyed by the author). —शौनक-गृह्य-सूत्र, अम्, n. the Gṛhya-sūtras of the Ṛg-veda ascribed to Śaunaka. —शौनकानुक्रमणी (°क-अन्°), f. an Anukra-maṇī or Vedic index ascribed to Śaunaka. —शौन-कारण्यक (°क-आर्°), अम्, n. an Āraṇyaka ascribed to Śaunaka (probably identified with the Aitareyā-raṇyaka). —शौनकोपनिषद् (°क-उप्°), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.
शौनकिन्: शौनकिन्, इनस्, m. pl. the pupils or followers of Śaunaka.
शौनकीपुत्र: शौनकी-पुत्र, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
शौनकीय: शौनकीय, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to or composed by Śaunaka or the Śaunakīyas, (शौनकीय-च-तुराध्यायिका, ‘Śaunaka's treatise in four chapters,’ i. e. the Atharva-veda Prātiśākhya); (आस्), m. pl. the pupils or school of Śaunaka. —शौनकीय-च-तुराध्यायिका, f., N. of the above Prātiśākhya. —शौनकीय-चरण, N. of a Caraṇa (probably founded by the author of the Śākala-prātiśākhya).
शौनहोत्र: शौनहोत्र शौनहोत्र, अस्, m. the son of Śuna-hotra and grandson of Bharad-vāja; epithet of the Vedic Ṛṣi Gṛtsa-mada.
शौभ: शौभ शौभ, अस्, m. (fr. शुभ), a god, di-vinity; the Areca or betel-nut tree (= गुवाक); (अम्), n. the city of Hariścandra (fabled to be sus-pended in the air, see हरि-श्-चन्द्र).
शौभनेय: शौभनेय शौभनेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शोभना), sprung from a handsome mother; relating to any-thing handsome or brilliant.
शौभाञ्जन: शौभाञ्जन शौभाञ्जन, अस्, m. (fr. शोभाञ्-जन, q. v.), the tree Hyperanthera Moringa.
शौभिक: शौभिक शौभिक, अस्, m. (probably con-nected with शुभ), a juggler, conjurer (= इन्द्र-जालिक).
शौभ्रेय: शौभ्रेय शौभ्रेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or be-longing to anything white or shining (e. g. to silver, talc, sandal, &c.); (अस्), m. ‘son of Śubhrā,’ a patro-nymic.
शौर: शौर शौर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूर), relating to a hero, heroic.
शौरदेव्य: शौरदेव्यः, in Ṛg-veda VIII. 70, 15. appa-rently acc. pl. of शौरदेवी, qualifying गाः, ‘cows,’ and explained by Sāy. thus, दीव्यन्ति क्रीडन्त इति देवा योद्धारः शूराश्-च ते देवाश्-च शूर-देवाः, तेषां हितं शौरदेवं युद्धं तत्-सम्-बन्धिन्यो गाः।
शौरदेव्यः: शौरदेव्यः, in Ṛg-veda VIII. 70, 15. appa-rently acc. pl. of शौरदेवी, qualifying गाः, ‘cows,’ and explained by Sāy. thus, दीव्यन्ति क्रीडन्त इति देवा योद्धारः शूराश्-च ते देवाश्-च शूर-देवाः, तेषां हितं शौरदेवं युद्धं तत्-सम्-बन्धिन्यो गाः।
शौरसेन: शौरसेन, अम्, n. (fr. शूर-सेन), the language spoken by the people of Śūra-sena; (ई), f. a Prākṛt dialect supposed to have been spoken at Mathurā.
शौरि: शौरि, इस्, m., N. of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa; of Bala-rāma (as descended from Śūra); the planet Saturn.
शौर्य: शौर्य, अम्, n. heroism, valour, prowess, might; the heroic branch of the dramatic art, representation of war and supernatural events on the stage (= आर-भटी). —शौर्योपार्जित (°य-उप्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ac-quired by valour.
शौर्प: शौर्प शौर्प, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शूर्प), measured by a winnowing basket &c., belonging to a winnow-ing fan &c.
शौर्पणाय्य: शौर्पणाय्य, अस्, m., N. of a preceptor.
शौर्पिक: शौर्पिक, अस्, ई, अम्, = शौर्प above.
शौल्क: शौल्क शौल्क, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुल्क), relating to tolls or customs or taxes, levied (as a tax &c.); (अस्), m. a superintendant of tolls or customs, a custom-house officer.
शौल्कशालिक: शौल्कशालिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुल्क-शाला), of or belonging to a custom-house, derived from a custom-house.
शौल्कायनि: शौल्कायनि, इस्, m., N. of a Muni.
शौल्किक: शौल्किक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to taxes or tolls; (अस्), m. a superintendant of tolls or customs.
शौल्किकेय: शौल्किकेय शौल्किकेय, अस्, m. (fr. शुल्किक), a kind of poison (said to be produced in a country called Śulkika; according to some the venom of a kind of snake).
शौल्फ: शौल्फ शौल्फ, अम्, n. a kind of vegetable (commonly called Śulphā).
शौल्विक: शौल्विक शौल्विक, अस्, m. (fr. शुल्व), a cop-persmith.
शौव: शौव शौव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. श्वन्), relating or belonging to dogs, canine; (अस्), m., N. of a par-ticular Udgītha; (अम्), n. a pack or number of dogs; the nature or state of a dog.
शौवन: शौवन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to canine nature; having the qualities of a dog; (अम्), n. the nature of a dog; the progeny of a dog.
शौवापद: शौवापद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. श्वा-पद), relating to a wild beast or beast of prey, ferocious, savage, wild.
शौवस्तिक: शौवस्तिक शौवस्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. श्वस्), of or belonging to to-morrow, lasting till to-morrow, ephemeral. —शौवस्तिक-त्व, अम्, n. the lasting or enduring till to-morrow, ephemeralness.
शौष्कल: शौष्कल शौष्कल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. शुष्कली), eating fish and flesh; (अस्), m. an habitual eater of meat; a vender of flesh, dealer in flesh or dried meat; (अम्), n. the price of dried meat.
श्चम्: श्चम् श्चम्, for rt. चम्, to consume, (ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 104, 2. श्चम्नन् = भक्षयन्तु, but also referrible to rt. 1. शम्।)

श्चोत: श्चोत or श्च्योत, अस्, m. oozing, trickling out, sprinkling, aspersion, pouring forth.

श्नथितृ: श्नथितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who slays or kills, a smiter; killing, destroying, destructive, deadly, fatal.
श्नम्: श्नम् श्नम्, (in grammar) a technical term for the verbal affix न, the characteristic sign of the seventh class of roots.

श्यान, अस्, आ, अम्, gone; coagulated, congealed; viscous, thick, sticky, adhesive (as clarified butter); shrunk up, shrunk; (अम्), n. smoke. —श्यान-पुलिन, अस्, आ, अम्, having shrunk or dry sand-banks (as a river in the hot season).

श्यापर्णेय: श्यापर्णेय, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ. VI. 2, 37.
