श्लाघन: श्लाघन, अम्, n. the act of flattering, praising, &c.
श्लाघनीय: श्लाघनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised, praise-worthy, laudable, commendable.
श्लाघमान: श्लाघमान, अस्, आ, अम्, flattering, praising; con-gratulating one's self, rejoicing.
श्लाघयित्वा: श्लाघयित्वा, ind. having praised or applauded.
श्लाघा: श्लाघा, f. flattery, praise, commendation, pane-gyric, eulogium; boasting; service, obedience; wish, desire. —श्लाघा-वह, अस्, आ, अम्, meriting praise.
श्लाघित: श्लाघित, अस्, आ, अम्, flattered, praised, commended.
श्लाघित्वा: श्लाघित्वा, ind. having flattered, having praised, &c.
श्लाघिन्: श्लाघिन्, ई, इनी, इ, flattering, praising, commend-ing; desiring.
श्लाघ्य: श्लाघ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised or commended, praiseworthy, entitled to praise or veneration, venera-ble, respectable, honourable.
श्लाघ्यमान: श्लाघ्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being praised, &c.
श्लिकु: श्लिकु श्लिकु, उस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 33. fr. rt. 2. श्लिष्), a servant, slave, dependant; a profligate or low person, libertine, debauchee; (उ), n. astronomy, astrology.
श्लिष्: श्लिष् 1. श्लिष् (= rt. 1. श्रिष्), cl. 1. P. श्लेषति, शिश्लेष, श्लेषितुम्, to burn, consume by fire.

श्लिष् 2. श्लिष्, cl. 4. P. श्लिष्यति (ep. also A. -ते), शिश्लेष, श्लेक्ष्यति, अश्लिक्षत् (in the sense of ‘to embrace’), अश्लि-षत् (and according to some also अश्लैक्षीत् in other senses), श्लेष्टुम्, to adhere, cling to, be united or connected with; to embrace; to unite, tie, join, connect: Pass. श्लिष्यते, Aor. अश्लेषि, to be joined or connected; to be implied or intimated; cl. 10. P. or Caus. श्लेषयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशि-श्लिषत्, to cause to embrace; to embrace, connect: Desid. शिश्लिक्षति: Intens. शेश्लिष्यते, शेश्लेष्टि; [cf. Gr. κλη-ΐς, κλείς, κλει-δός, κλεί-ω: Lat. clāvi-s, clau-d-o: Old Germ. sliuz-u: Slav. klju-ci, ‘a key;’ kljucati se, ‘to agree:’ Hib. crios, ‘a belt, girdle.’]
श्लेष: 2. श्लेष, अस्, m. adhering or clinging to; em-bracing, an embrace; union, junction, contact, prox-imity; association, society, presence; a figure of rhetoric, connection of words so as to admit of a double meaning, verbal equivocation, paronomasia, pun, irony, implied meaning. —श्लेष-भित्तिक, अस्, आ, अम्, resting on or adhering to a wall, (said to mean simply ‘resting on.’) —श्लेषार्थ (°ष-अर्°), अस्, m. a meaning other than the literal one, a second sense hidden in the obvious one, implied meaning.
श्लिषा: श्लिषा, f. clinging, embracing, an embrace.
श्लिष्ट: श्लिष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, clung to, adhered to; touched by; leaning on; embraced; connected so as to be sus-ceptible of a double interpretation, (applied to a figure of speech by which two objects are closely connected and epithets applied to both in common), implied.
श्लिष्टि: श्लिष्टि, इस्, f. adherence, connection; embrace; (इस्), m., N. of a son of Dhruva.
श्लिष्ट्वा: श्लिष्ट्वा, ind. having clung or adhered, having embraced.
श्लिष्यत्: श्लिष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, clinging to, adhering to, being in close contact with; embracing.
श्लिष्यमाण: श्लिष्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being embraced, &c.
श्लेषण: श्लेषण, अम्, n. the act of adhering, embracing, &c.
श्लेषणीय: श्लेषणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be embraced, &c.
श्लेषिन्: श्लेषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, adhering, clinging to, embracing.
श्लेष्मक: श्लेष्मक, अस्, m. phlegm, the watery or phleg-matic humor.
श्लेष्मण: श्लेष्मण, अस्, आ, अम्, phlegmatic; (आ), f. a kind of plant (= तर्पणी).
श्लेष्मन्: श्लेष्मन्, आ, m. phlegm, rheum, the phlegmatic humor, (one of the three humors of the body; see धातु।) —श्लेष्म-घ्न, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, removing phlegm; (आ), f. Arabian jasmine; a kind of tree (= केतक); (ई), f. Arabian jasmine; hogweed; another plant (= ज्योतिष्मती); the three spices (= त्रि-कटु). —श्लेष्म-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced or proceeding from phlegm. —श्लेष्म-धातु, उस्, m. the phlegmatic humor. —श्लेष्म-ह, अस्, आ, अम्, removing phlegm; (अस्), m. a medicinal plant (= कट्-फल). —श्लेष्मातिसार (°म-अत्°), अस्, m. dysentery or diarrhœa produced by vitiated phlegm. —श्लेष्मान्तक (°म-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘destroying phlegm,’ a kind of plant (= पिच्छिल, बहु-वार)। —श्लेष्माश्रु (°म-अश्°), उ, n. a tear consisting of phlegmatic humor. —श्लेष्मौजस् (°म-ओज्°), अस्, n. the phlegmatic humor.
श्लेष्मल: श्लेष्मल, अस्, आ, अम्, phlegmatic, abounding or affected with phlegm, &c.; (अस्), m. the plant Cordia Myxa or Latifolia.
श्लेष्मात: श्लेष्मात, अस्, m. a kind of tree, = श्लेष्मातक।
श्लेष्मातक: श्लेष्मातक, अस्, m. the tree Cordia Myxa. —श्ले-ष्मातक-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, made of Cordia Myxa. —श्लेष्मातक-वन, अम्, n. ‘forest of Śleṣmā-taka trees,’ N. of a forest about Go-karṇa (where Śiva is said to have been concealed in the form of a stag).
श्लैष्मिक: श्लैष्मिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to phlegm, phlegmatic; producing phlegm.
श्लीपद: श्लीपद श्लीपद, अम्, n. (thought by some to be fr. rt. 2. श्लिष् + पद), morbid enlargement of the leg, swelled leg, elephantiasis. —श्लीपद-प्र-भव, अस्, m. ‘source of elephantiasis,’ the Mango tree. —श्लीपदापह (°द-अप्°), अस्, m. ‘removing or curing elephantiasis,’ a kind of tree (= पुत्र-जीव).
श्लीपदिन्: श्लीपदिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a swelled leg, club-footed; (ई), m. a club-footed man.
श्लील: श्लील श्लील, अस्, आ, अम् (for श्रील), prosperous, fortunate, affluent, happy.
श्लु: श्लु श्लु, one of the three technical terms for grammatical elision classed with लुक्, q. v.
श्लोक्: श्लोक् श्लोक् (probably rather a Nom. fr. श्लोक below), cl. 1. A. श्लोकते, श्लोकि-तुम्, to versify, compose or make verses, hymn or praise in verse; to be put together or composed; to acquire; to relinquish, abandon.
श्लोक: श्लोक, अस्, m. (probably connected with rt. 1. श्रु; according to Rāmāyaṇa I. 2, 33. fr. शोक, ‘sorrow,’ the first Śloka having resulted from the involuntary expression of Vālmīki's grief at be-holding a bird killed by a fowler), praising or hymning in verse, a hymn of praise; an object of praise; celebrity, renown, fame, reputation; a par-ticular kind of common epic metre (also called Anu-ṣṭubh, consisting of four Pādas or quarter verses of eight syllables each, or two lines of sixteen syllables each; the following is the usual scheme applicable to both lines ....˘˘˘. | ....˘¯˘. , the mark. denoting either long or short, and the sixth syllable being either short or long, but if short, then requiring the seventh to be short also, and if long, then long); any verse or stanza; a proverb, saying; = वाच् (Naigh. I. 11). —श्लोक-ता, f. or श्लोक-त्व, अम्, n. versification; celebrity in verse. —श्लोक-द्वय, अम्, n. a couple of Ślokas, two verses. —श्लोक-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, composed in Ślokas. —श्लोक-मात्र, अम्, n. a single Śloka.
श्लोकय: श्लोकय, Nom. P. श्लोकयति, -यितुम्, to celebrate in song.
श्लोकिन्: श्लोकिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. having hymns of praise, receiving praise, praised, lauded.
श्लोक्य: श्लोक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in hymns of praise, be-longing to Ślokas.
श्लोण्: श्लोण् श्लोण् (also written श्रोण्), cl. 1. P. श्लोणति, श्लोणितुम्, to accumulate, col-lect, assemble, heap together: Caus. श्लोणयति, -यि-तुम्, Aor. अशुश्लोणत्।
श्लोण: श्लोण श्लोण, अस्, m. (= श्रोण; cf. अ-श्लोण), a lame man, cripple.
श्वघ्निन्: श्वघ्निन्, ई, m. (according to some श्व is for स्व, and the word is thought to mean ‘one who destroys his own,’ others connect it with श्व-हन्), Ved. a gamester, (Sāy. = देवन-शील।)
श्वङ्क्: श्वङ्क् श्वङ्क् (also written स्वङ्क्), cl. 1. A. श्वङ्कते, शश्वङ्के, श्वङ्कितुम्, to go, move.
श्वङ्ग्: श्वङ्ग् श्वङ्ग् (also written श्रङ्ग्, स्वङ्ग्, &c.; cf. rt. श्वङ्क्), cl. 1. P. श्वङ्गति, श्वङ्गितुम्, to go, move.
श्वच्: श्वच् श्वच् or श्वञ्च् (= rts. शञ्च्, श्वज्), cl. 1. A. श्वचते, श्वञ्चते, &c., (Ved. form श्वञ्चयः, Ṛg-veda X. 138, 2; शश्वचै, see s. v.), to go, move; to gape, open, be opened, be split.
श्वज्: श्वज् श्वज् or श्वञ्ज् (= rts. श्वच्, शञ्च्), cl. 1. A. श्वजते, श्वञ्जते, &c., to go, move.
श्वञ्च्: श्वञ्च् श्वञ्च्। See above under rt. श्वच्।
श्वठ्: श्वठ् 1. श्वठ् (= rt. 2. शठ्), cl. 10. P. श्वठयति, -यितुम्, to speak ill; (ac-cording to some) to speak well or correctly; to be accurate or true.
श्वठ् 2. श्वठ् or श्वण्ठ् (= rts. 3. शठ्, स्वठ्, सठ्), cl. 10. P. श्वाठयति, श्वण्-ठयति, &c., -यितुम्, to finish, accomplish, adorn; to leave unfinished or unornamented; to go, move.
श्वन्: श्वन् श्वन्, आ, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. I. 158. fr. rt. श्वि, perhaps fr. a participial base श्वन्त्; Nom. sing. du. pl. श्वा, श्वानौ, श्वानस्; Acc. श्वा-नम्, श्वानौ, शुनस्; Inst. शुना, श्वभ्याम्, &c., Gram. 155. a), a dog, hound, cur; (शुनी), f. a female dog, bitch. श्वन् becomes श्वा for श्व in some com-pounds, see below; [cf. Zend śpâ; Gr. κύ-ων, κυνός (= शुनस्), ἁλ-κυών; Lat. can-i-s (for cvan-i-s), catulus; Goth. hun-d-s; Lith. nom. szu§, gen. szuns; Hib. nom. cu, gen. and pl. coin; Russ. sobaka (for shaka); Pers. sag.] —श्व-किष्किन्, ई, इणी, इ, Ved. (according to some) having the tail of a dog, (Sāy. connects किष्किन् with किष्कु, ‘a staff, thunderbolt,’ Atharva-veda VIII. 6, 6.) —श्व-क्री-डिन्, ई, m. one who sports with dogs, a dog-feeder or trainer, a breeder of sporting dogs. —श्व-गण, अस्, m. a pack or collection of dogs. —श्वगणिक, अस्, m. ‘one who has to do with packs of dogs,’ a hunter; (अस्, ई), m. f. a dog-feeder; one who is drawn by dogs. —श्व-गणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having packs of hounds. —श्व-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘dog-seizure,’ epithet of a particular disease or the deity presiding over it. —श्व-घ्नी, see under श्व-हन्. —श्व-चाण्-डाल, अम्, n. a dog and an outcast. —श्व-चिल्ली, f. a kind of pot-herb (= शुनक-चिल्ली). —श्व-जा-घनी, f. a dog's thigh, the haunch of a dog, (Manu X. 108.) —श्व-दंष्ट्रक, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= गो-क्षुर). —श्व-दंष्ट्रा, f. a dog's tooth; a kind of plant (= गो-क्षुर). —श्व-धूर्-त, अस्, m. ‘dog-rogue,’ a jackal. —श्व-नर, अस्, m. a dog-like fellow, low fellow, currish or snappish fellow. —श्व-निश, अम्, आ, n. f. ‘dog-night,’ a night on which dogs bark and howl. —श्व-पच्, क्, or श्व-पच, अस्, आ, m. f. ‘dog-cooking,’ a man or woman of a low and degraded caste, (see श्व-पाक); a public executioner; a dog-feeder, dog-keeper; (ई), f. a form of one of the Śaktis of Śiva. —श्व-पद, अम्, n. a dog's foot; a mark like a dog's foot to be branded on the forehead of a thief. —श्व-पाक, अस्, m. ‘dog-cooking,’ a man of a degraded and outcast tribe (described as son of an Ugra woman by a Kṣatriya, and classed with the Caṇḍāla, q. v.; he is required to live outside towns, to eat his food in broken vessels, to wear the clothes of the dead, and to be excluded from all intercourse with other tribes; he can possess no other property than asses and dogs, and his only office is to act as public executioner or to carry out the bodies of those who die without kindred); (ई), f. a woman of the above low or out-cast tribe. —श्व-फल, अम्, n. the lime or common citron. —श्व-फल्क, अस्, m., N. of the son of Pṛśni (or according to others of Vṛṣṇi; he was husband of Gāndinī, by whom he had a son named Akrūra). —श्व-भीरु, उस्, m. ‘dog-fearing,’ a jackal. —श्व-भोजन, अस्, m. ‘having dogs for food,’ N. of a Naraka. —श्व-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a demon in the shape of a dog. —श्व-यूथ्य, अम्, n. a number or pack of dogs. —श्व-रूप-धारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, wearing or having the form of a dog. —१। श्व-वत्, आन्, m. possessing or keeping a dog, a dog-feeder, dog-trainer. —२। श्व-वत्, ind. like a dog, cur-like. —श्व-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the life of a dog; condition of a dog; service, servitude (which a Brāhman ought not to engage in). —श्व-व्याघ्र, अस्, m. a beast of prey, a tiger; the hunting leopard or Chīta. —श्व-सुत, अस्, m. the plant Conyza Aspera. —श्व-स्पृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, touched by a dog, defiled. —श्व-हत, अस्, आ, अम्, killed by a dog, killed by dogs. —श्व-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, Ved. one who kills with dogs; (आ), m. a hunter; (घ्नी), f. the wife of a hunter. —श्वा-कर्ण, अस्, m. a dog's ear. —श्वा-दन्त, अस्, m. (श्वा for श्व), a dog's tooth. —श्वा-पद, अस्, m. a beast of prey, wild beast; a tiger; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating or belonging to a wild beast, ferocious, savage, (in this sense properly an adj. fr. श्वा-पद, and therefore to be written without a hyphen.) —श्वापद-सेवित, अस्, आ, अम्, frequented or infested by wild beasts. —श्वापदा-चरित (°द-आच्°), अस्, आ, अम्, overrun or infested by wild beasts. —श्वापदानुसरण (°द-अन्°), अम्, n. the pursuit or chase after a wild animal. —श्वा-पुच्छ, अस्, अम्, m. n. a dog's tail. —श्वाविच्-छरण, अम्, n. (i. e. श्वा-विध्, see below, + शर-ण), the lair or resting-place of a porcupine, (a porcupine's hole has always two or more entrances.) —श्वा-विध्, त्, m. (श्वा for श्व), a porcupine, hedge-hog. —श्वाश्व (श्व-अश्°), अस्, m. ‘having a dog for a horse,’ epithet of Bhairava (or Śiva in a ter-rific form, sometimes represented as mounted on a dog).
श्व: श्व at the end of comps. = श्वन् above.
श्वागणिक: श्वागणिक, अस्, m. (fr. श्व-गण), one who has to do with packs of dogs, a hunter; (अस्, ई), m. f. one who lives by feeding or keeping dogs, a dog-keeper; one who is drawn by dogs.
श्वान: श्वान, अस्, m. a dog; the wind, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 161, 13. श्वानम् = अन्तरिक्षे श्वसन्तं वायुम्); (ई), f. a female dog, bitch. —श्वान-चिल्लिका, f. a kind of pot-herb. —श्वान-निद्रा, f. a dog's sleep; light slumber. —श्वान-वैखरी, f. ‘dog's speech,’ a term for angry snarling on trifling occasions. —श्वानोच्छिष्ट (°न-उच्°), अम्, n. anything left by a dog.
श्वभ्र्: श्वभ्र् श्वभ्र् [cf. rt. श्वर्त्], cl. 10. P. श्व-भ्रयति, -यितुम्, to go, move; to live in misery (in a hole?); to break, pierce, bore, make a hole.
श्वभ्र: श्वभ्र, अम्, n. a hole, gap, chasm; a den.
श्वयथु: श्वयथु श्वयथु, श्वयीचि। See under rt. श्वि।
श्वयथु, उस्, m. swelling, intumescence. —श्वय-थु-चिकित्सा, f. the cure or treatment of swellings, &c.
श्वर्त्: श्वर्त् श्वर्त् (also written स्वर्त्; cf. rt. श्वभ्र्), cl. 10. P. श्वर्तयति, &c., -यि-तुम्, to go, move; to live in misery or distress.
श्वल्: श्वल् श्वल् or श्वल्ल्, cl. 1. P. श्वलति or श्वल्लति, शश्वाल or शश्वल्ल, श्वलितुम् or श्वल्लितुम्, to go quickly, run.
श्वल्क्: श्वल्क् श्वल्क् [cf. rt. शुल्क्], cl. 10. P. श्वल्-कयति, -यितुम्, to tell, narrate.
श्वशुर: श्वशुर श्वशुर, अस्, m. (perhaps for original स्व-शुर, see शुर; in Uṇādi-s. I. 45. said to be fr. rt. 1. अश् with शु for आशु prefixed), a father-in-law, a wife's or husband's father; one to be treated as a father-in-law, a venerable man; a proper N.; (औ), m. du. a father and mother-in-law; [cf. Zend qaśura; Gr. ἑκυρό-ς for σϝεκυρό-ς; Lat. socer for svecer; Goth. svaihra; Old Germ. svehur; Angl. Sax. sweger, sweor; Slav. svekru; Lith. szeszura-s; Cambro-Brit. cwegrwn.]
श्वशुर्य: श्वशुर्य, अस्, m. a brother-in-law, wife's brother, husband's brother; a husband's younger brother.
श्वश्रू: श्वश्रू, ऊस्, f. a mother-in-law; [cf. Gr. ἔκυρα; Lat. socrus; Goth. svaihrô; Old Germ. suigar; Cambro-Brit. çwegyr; Slav. svekruvi or svekry; perhaps Lith. u§szwe†.] —श्वश्रू-श्वशुर, औ, m. du. mother and father-in-law.
श्वस्: श्वस् 1. श्वस्, cl. 2. P. श्वसिति, (also ap-parently cl. 1. P. A. श्वसति, -ते, in certain forms and according to a various reading in Naigh. II. 19), Impf. अश्वसीत् or अश्वसत् (Pāṇ. VII. 3, 98, 99, cf. rt. 1. रुद्), Pot. श्वसेत् (cl. 1), Impv. श्व-सितु (or श्वसतु, 2nd pl. A. श्वसध्वम्), श-श्वास, श्वसिष्यति, अश्वसीत्, श्वसितुम्, to breathe, respire, draw breath, live, pant, puff, sigh; to hiss, snort; to strike, kill, (enumerated among the वध-कर्माणः in Naigh. II. 19): Caus. श्वासयति, यितुम्, Aor. अशिश्वसत्, to cause to breathe easily, to refresh: Desid. शिश्वसिषति: Intens. शाश्वस्यते, शाश्वस्ति, to breathe frequently, pant; [cf. Lat. queri, ques-tus; Angl. Sax. hweosan, perhaps hysian, hyst, gist.]

श्वस् 2. श्वस्, ind. (according to some con-nected with a lost rt. श्वि in श्वित्, ‘to be white,’ and originally denoting ‘the morrow's dawn’), to-morrow; future, (at the beginning of a comp.); future happiness or fortune, (apparently used in this sense at the beginning of certain comps.); a particle implying auspiciousness; [cf. Lat. cras.] —श्वः-श्रेयस, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘happy in the future,’ happy, prosperous; (अम्), n. happiness, prosperity; Brahma, the Supreme Spirit; (अम्), ind. happy, well, right. —श्वः-सुत्या, f., Ved. to-morrow's preparation of the Soma. —श्वो-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, being to-morrow; (ए), ind. on its being to-morrow. —श्वो-वसीय, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘happy for all future time,’ auspicious, fortunate; (अम्), n. happiness. —श्वो-वसीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, fortunate, prosperous, auspicious. —श्वो-वसीयस, अस्, आ, अम्, fortunate, auspicious; (अम्), n. auspicious-ness, good fortune. —श्वो-वस्यस, अम्, n., Ved., N. of Brahma.
श्वसत्: श्वसत्, अन्, अती (ep. also अन्ती), अत्, breathing, sighing.
श्वसन: श्वसन, अस्, m. air, wind; epithet of a demon of drought vanquished by Indra [cf. शुष्ण]; the thorny plant Vangueria Spinosa; (अम्), n. breathing, respiration, breath; sighing. —श्वसनासन (°न-अस्°), अस्, m. ‘air-eater, breath-eater,’ a snake, serpent. —श्वसनेश्वर (°न-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘breath-lord,’ the tree Pentaptera Arjuna. —श्वसनोत्सुक (°न-उत्°), अस्, m. ‘eager for air’ or ‘fond of hissing,’ a snake. —श्वसनोर्मि (°न-ऊर्°), इस्, m. f. a wave or gust of wind.
श्वसमान: श्वसमान, अस्, आ, अम्, breathing; panting, snorting, hissing.
श्वसित: श्वसित, अस्, आ, अम्, breathed, sighed; breathing, sighing; (अम्), n. breathing, breath, respiration, sighing, a sigh.
श्वसीवत्: श्वसी-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. possessed of breath, vivifying, (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 140, 10. श्वसीवान् = श्वसन-वान् ज्वालाभिश् चेष्टा-वान् प्राणन-वान् वा।)
श्वसुन: श्वसुन, अस्, m. a kind of plant (= क्षत-घ्न).
श्वास: श्वास, अस्, m. breathing, breath, inspiration, re-spiration; sighing, a sigh; air, wind; affection of the breath, hard breathing, asthma. —श्वास-कास, अस्, m. ‘breath-cough,’ asthma. —श्वास-कुठार, अस्, m. a particular drug used as a remedy for asthma. —श्वास-ता, f. breathing, respiration, aspiration. —श्वास-प्रश्वास-धारण, अम्, n. suppression or suspension of inspiration and expiration (= प्राणा-याम, q. v.). —श्वास-रोध, अस्, m. an obstruction of the breath. —श्वास-हिक्का, f. a kind of hiccough. —श्वास-हेति, इस्, f. ‘cure for hard breathing,’ sleepi-ness, sleep. —श्वासारि (°स-अरि), इस्, m. ‘breath-enemy,’ a kind of plant (= पुष्कर-मूल). —श्वा-सोच्छ्वास (°स-उच्°), औ, m. du. inspiration and ex-piration, respiration.
श्वासित: श्वासित, अस्, आ, अम्, caused to breathe, refreshed, invigorated.
श्वासिन्: श्वासिन्, ई, इनी, इ, breathing, respiring; (ई), m. air, wind.
श्वस्तन: श्वस्तन, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to the morrow, what will be to-morrow, future; (अम्), n. the future [cf. Lat. crastinus]; (ई), f., scil. विभक्ति, a gram-matical term for the personal terminations of the first future.
श्वस्त्य: श्वस्त्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to the morrow, what will be to-morrow, future.
श्वात्र: श्वात्र 1. श्वात्र, अस्, आ, अम् (probably fr. rt. श्वि; cf. शवस्, शिव), Ved. increasing, powerful, strong, flourishing, blooming (according to some); quick, swift, (Sāy. = क्षिप्र-धर्मक, Ṛg-veda X. 46, 7); (अम्), ind. quickly, (Sāy. = क्षिप्रम्); (अम्), n. prosperity, riches, wealth. —श्वात्र-भाज्, क्, क्, क्, Ved. wealth-associated, endowed with riches.
2. श्वात्र, Nom. P. श्वात्रति, &c., Ved. to go, hasten, (enumerated among the गति-कर्माणः in Naigh. II. 14.)
श्वात्र्य: श्वात्र्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. causing prosperity or happiness, (Sāy. = सुखावह); going quickly, (Sāy. = क्षिप्र-गमनार्ह।)
श्वान्त: श्वान्त श्वान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. wearied; placid, (Sāy. = श्रान्त or शान्त, Ṛg-veda I. 145, 4.)
श्वापद: श्वापद श्वा-पद, श्वा-विध्, &c. See under श्वन्।
श्वाशुरि: श्वाशुरि श्वाशुरि, इस्, m. (fr. श्वशुर), a patronymic.
श्वि: श्वि श्वि (this rt. assumes the form शु, q. v., in some of its tenses and derivatives; cf. rt. शव्), cl. 1. P. श्वयति, शुशाव or शिश्वाय (2nd sing. शुशविथ or शिश्वयिथ, 3rd du. शुशु-वतुस् or शिश्वियतुस्), श्वयिष्यति, अश्वयीत् or अश्वत् or अशिश्वियत्, Prec. शूयात्, श्वयितुम्, to swell, increase, grow; to thrive; to appear (Ved., see वि-श्वि, referred by some to rt. श्वित्); to go, ap-proach: Pass. शूयते, Aor. अश्वायि: Caus. श्वाय-यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अशूशवत् or अशिश्वयत्, (accord-ing to others also अशीशवत्): Desid. of Caus. शुशा-वयिषति or शिश्वाययिषति, to cause to swell or grow or be prosperous: Desid. शिश्वयिषति: Intens. शेश्वीयते, शोशूयते, शेश्वयीति, शेश्वेति, to swell much; [cf. Gr. κυ-έ-ω, κύ-ος, κῦ-μα, κύ-η-μα, κύ-αρ, κύ-τ-ος, κοῖ-λο-ς, κοιλ-ία, καυλό-ς, κύ-λο-ν, ἐγ-κισσάω, κίσσα, κύαμος, κύαθος, κῶνος, κηκίς, κίκυς, (probably also) κίων, κίω, κινέω, perhaps also κό-μη (for κύ-μη): Lat. in-ci-ens, cu-mu-lu-s, cavu-s, cau-li-s, cau-lœ, cœlu-m, ciliu-m, super-cili-um, cuneus, crescere; coma: Goth. us-hul-on, hul-undi: Old Germ. hol, (according to some) wī-t, ‘wide’ (= श्वित): Angl. Sax. hol: Hib. cin-neas, cinneachdin, ‘growth, increase.’]
शूयमन: शूयमन, अस्, आ, अम्, being swollen, swelling, enlarging, expanding.
श्वयित्वा: श्वयित्वा, ind. having swelled or increased.
श्विक्न: श्विक्न श्विक्न, आस्, m. pl., N. of a race; [cf. श्वैक्न।]
श्वित्: श्वित् श्वित् (perhaps a kind of Nom. based on a lost rt. श्वि, cf. Zend śpi-तम, &c.), cl. 1. A. श्वेतते (Ved. also P. -ति), शिश्विते, श्वेतिष्यते, अश्वेतिष्ट, अश्वितत्, श्वेतितुम्, to be or become white, (according to Vopa-deva XXI. 15. श्वेतयति = श्वेताश्वम् आचष्टे); [cf. Lith. swe†ciu for swetiu, ‘I shine;’ Inf. swe†sti for swe†t-ti, (perhaps also) swe†ta-s, ‘the world;’ kaiciu for kaitiu, kaitinu, ‘I make hot;’ kais-tu for kait-tu, ‘I become warm;’ kaitau: Slav. svit-a-ti, ‘to become light;’ swjet, ‘light, the world.’]
श्वित: श्वित, अस्, आ, अम्, white; (अम्), n. whiteness (according to Sāy.).
श्वितान: श्वितान, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being white, white-coloured, (Sāy. = श्वेतमान, श्वेत-वर्ण, Ṛg-veda VI. 6, 2.)
श्विति: श्विति, whiteness, a white colour (according to Sāy.). —श्वित्य्-अञ्च्, अङ्, -तीची, अक्, Ved. going to whiteness, becoming white, white-coloured, fair-com-plexioned, white, (Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 83, 8. श्वित्यञ्चः = श्वितं श्वैत्यं नैर्मल्यम् अञ्-चन्तो गच्छन्तः।)
श्वित्त: श्वित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, see Pāṇ. VII. 2, 16, 17.
श्वित्न: श्वित्न, white (according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 100, 18).
श्वित्न्य: श्वित्न्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. white, white-coloured, fair-complexioned (said of the winds or Maruts ac-cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 100, 18; but accord-ing to some more probably referring to the fair-coloured worshippers of Indra as opposed to the darker aborigines of India).
श्वित्य: श्वित्य, अस्, आ, अम्, white, white-coloured.
श्वित्र: श्वित्र, अम्, n. morbid whiteness of the skin, white leprosy, vitiligo; = अन्तरिक्ष (Ved., cf. श्वैत्रेय); (आ), f. a proper N. —श्वित्र-घ्नी, f. ‘removing whiteness of the skin,’ the plant Tragia Involucrata (= पीत-पर्णी).
श्वित्रिन्: श्वित्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, affected with whiteness of the skin or leprosy, leprous; (ई), m. a leper.
श्वित्र्य: श्वित्र्य, अस्, m., Ved. a son of Śvitrā.
श्वेत: श्वेत, अस्, आ or श्वेनी, अम्, white, dressed in white; (अस्), m. white (the colour); the planet Venus or its regent Śukra; the sixth range of mountains dividing the known continent, the white mountains separating the Varṣas of Hiraṇmaya and Ramyaka; one of the minor Dvīpas or divisions of the world, (see श्वेत-द्वीप); a white cloud; cumin seed; a conch-shell; N. of a particular Avatāra of Śiva; of a manifestation of Viṣṇu in his Varāha incarnation (worshipped in a particular part of India); N. of one of Śiva's pupils; (अस्, आ), m. f. a small white shell, cowri; (आ), f. one of the tongues of Fire; a kind of grass, Andropogon Aciculatum; a kind of plant (= काष्ठ-पाटला); Aconitum Ferox; various other plants (= अपराजिता; = श्वेत-वृहती; = श्वेत-कण्टकारी; = पाषाण-भेदिन्; = शिला-वल्कला; = छूरिका-पत्त्री); hogweed; white Dūrvā grass; bamboo-manna; crystal; clayed or candied sugar; a mystical term for the letter स्; (अम्), n. silver; (श्वेत वैदार्व or वैदार्व्य or वैदर्व्य is according to some ‘a serpent demon,’ others give श्वैत-वैदारव as signifying ‘a particular deity connected with the sun’); [cf. Goth. hveit-s, ‘white;’ (perhaps) hvaitei, ‘wheat:’ Old Germ. huiz, wīz: Old Sax., Angl. श्वेतक: श्वेतक, अस्, m. a cowri; (अम्), n. silver.
श्वेतना: श्वेतना, f., Ved. ‘the whitener,’ epithet of Uṣas or dawn.
श्वेतयत्: श्वेतयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, making white, whitening.
श्वेतित: श्वेतित, अस्, आ, अम्, (probably) whitened, see Pāṇ. VII. 2, 16, 17.
श्वेती: श्वेती, f., N. of a river.

श्वेत्र: श्वेत्र, अम्, n. white leprosy (= श्वित्र).

श्वैत्र: श्वैत्र, अम्, n. white leprosy; vitiligo.
श्वैत्रेय: श्वैत्रेय, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. produced in the atmosphere; (अस्), m. = श्वित्र्य।
श्वैत्र्य: श्वैत्र्य, अम्, n. leprosy, whiteness of the skin.
